title.en: Volume 42 Biographies 34: Xiao Hui; Xiao Shiyi; Xiao Yuansu; Xiao Dahuan; Zong Lin; Liu Fan; Liu Xia
title.raw: 卷42 列傳第34 蕭撝 蕭世怡 蕭圓肅 蕭大圜 宗懍 劉璠 柳霞 Volume 42 Biographies 34: Xiao Hui; Xiao Shiyi; Xiao Yuansu; Xiao Dahuan; Zong Lin; Liu Fan; Liu Xia

sentences.zh: 蕭撝 蕭世怡 蕭圓肅 蕭大圜 宗懍 劉璠 柳霞

translations.literal: Xiao Hui; Xiao Shiyi; Xiao Yuansu; Xiao Dahuan; Zong Lin; Liu Fan; Liu Xia
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Xiao Hui, Xiao Shiyi, Xiao Yuansu, Xiao Dahuan, Zong Lin, Liu Fan, and Liu Xia

sentences.zh: 蕭撝字智遐，蘭陵人也。

translations.literal: Xiao Hui, courtesy name Zhixia, was a man of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Hui, whose courtesy name was Zhixia, came from Lanling.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝弟安成王秀之子也。

translations.literal: He was a son of Prince Ancheng Xiu, younger brother of Emperor Wu of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of Prince Ancheng Xiu, a younger brother of Emperor Wu of Liang.

sentences.zh: 性溫裕，有儀表。

translations.literal: His nature was gentle and generous, and he had a dignified bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and open-handed by temperament, he carried himself with notable dignity.

sentences.zh: 年十二，入國學，博觀經史，雅好屬文。

translations.literal: At age twelve he entered the Imperial Academy, read widely in the classics and histories, and was fond of literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: When he was twelve he entered the Imperial Academy, where he read widely in the classics and histories and took a keen delight in writing.

sentences.zh: 在梁，封永豐縣侯，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Under the Liang he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongfeng with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liang dynasty he was created Marquis of Yongfeng with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 初為給事中，歷太子洗馬、中舍人。

translations.literal: He first served as Attendant Within the Gates, then successively as Groom of the Heir Apparent and Palace Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He began as an Attendant Within the Gates and later held the posts of Groom of the Heir Apparent and Palace Attendant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 東魏遣李諧、盧元明使於梁，梁武帝以撝辭令可觀，令兼中書侍郎，受幣於賓館。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei sent Li Xie and Lu Yuanming as envoys to Liang; Emperor Wu of Liang, finding Hui's eloquence admirable, ordered him to serve concurrently as Vice Director of the Secretariat and to receive the tribute gifts at the guest house.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Wei sent Li Xie and Lu Yuanming as envoys to Liang, Emperor Wu judged Hui's command of diplomatic language impressive and had him serve concurrently as Vice Director of the Secretariat to receive the tribute gifts at the reception hall.

sentences.zh: 尋遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 出為寧遠將軍、宋寧宋興二郡守，轉輕車將軍、巴西梓潼二郡守。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the Distant, Administrator of the two commanderies of Songning and Songxing, then transferred to General of the Light Chariots, Administrator of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital as General Who Pacifies the Distant and administrator of Songning and Songxing, then became General of the Light Chariots and administrator of Baxi and Zitong.

sentences.zh: 及侯景作亂，武陵王紀承制授撝使持節、忠武將軍。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rose in rebellion, Prince Wuling Ji, acting under an imperial commission, appointed Hui Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Loyal Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing rebelled, Prince Wuling Ji, exercising imperial authority, appointed Hui Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Loyal Martial General.

sentences.zh: 又遷平北將軍、散騎常侍，領益州刺史軍防事。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to General Who Pacifies the North and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and put in charge of the military defense of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was next promoted to General Who Pacifies the North and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, with responsibility for the military defense of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 紀稱尊號於成都，除侍中、中書令，封秦郡王，邑三千戶，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: When Ji assumed an imperial title at Chengdu, Hui was appointed Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Prince of Qin with a fief of three thousand households, and granted one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: After Ji declared himself emperor at Chengdu, Hui was made Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat, created Prince of Qin with a fief of three thousand households, and granted a full ensemble of martial music.

sentences.zh: 紀率衆東下，以撝為

translations.literal: Ji led his forces eastward and appointed Hui as
translations.idiomatic: As Ji marched east at the head of his army, he appointed Hui

translations.literal: (Central)
translations.idiomatic: (the character 中, here emended to 尚)

sentences.zh: 〔尚〕書令、征西大將軍、都督益梁秦潼安瀘青戎寧華信渠萬江新邑楚義十八州諸軍事、益州刺史，守成都。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of the eighteen prefectures of Yi, Liang, Qin, Tong, An, Lu, Qing, Rong, Ning, Hua, Xin, Qu, Wan, Jiang, Xinyi, Chu, and Yi, and Governor of Yi, to hold Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the eighteen prefectures of Yi, Liang, Qin, Tong, An, Lu, Qing, Rong, Ning, Hua, Xin, Qu, Wan, Jiang, Xinyi, Chu, and Yi, and Governor of Yi, with orders to hold Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 又令梁州刺史楊乾運守潼州。

translations.literal: Ji also ordered Yang Qianyun, Governor of Liang Province, to hold Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Yang Qianyun, the governor of Liang Province, to defend Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 太祖知蜀兵寡弱，遣大將軍尉遲迥總衆討之。

translations.literal: The Grand Patriarch knew that the Shu forces were few and weak, and dispatched the Grand General Yuchi Jiong to take overall command of the army to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that the Shu armies were few and weak, the Grand Patriarch sent the Grand General Yuchi Jiong to take overall command of a punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 及迥入劔閣，乾運以州降。

translations.literal: When Jiong entered Jian Pass, Qianyun surrendered the province.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jiong had passed through Jian Pass, Qianyun surrendered his province.

sentences.zh: 蜀中因是大駭，無復抗拒之志。

translations.literal: Shu was thereby greatly terrified, and no longer had any will to resist.
translations.idiomatic: All of Shu was thrown into panic, and the will to resist collapsed.

sentences.zh: 迥長驅至成都，撝見兵不滿萬人，而倉庫空竭，軍無所資，遂為城守之計。

translations.literal: Jiong drove rapidly to Chengdu; Hui saw that his troops numbered fewer than ten thousand, while the storehouses were empty and the army had no supplies, and therefore adopted a plan of defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong marched straight to Chengdu. Finding fewer than ten thousand men under his command and the storehouses bare, with nothing left to supply the army, Hui resolved to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 迥圍之五旬，撝屢遣其將出城挑戰，多被殺傷。

translations.literal: Jiong besieged it for fifty days; Hui repeatedly sent his generals out to challenge battle, and many were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: After fifty days under siege, Hui repeatedly sent his generals out to offer battle, and many were killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 外援雖至，又為迥所破。

translations.literal: Although relief forces arrived, they were again defeated by Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Relief troops did arrive, but Jiong defeated them as well.

sentences.zh: 語在《迥傳》。

translations.literal: The account is given in the biography of Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: This is recounted in the biography of Jiong.

sentences.zh: 撝遂請降，迥許之。

translations.literal: Hui then requested surrender, and Jiong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then asked to surrender, and Jiong accepted.

sentences.zh: 撝於是率文武於益州城北，共迥升壇，歃血立盟，以城歸國。

translations.literal: Hui thereupon led the civil and military officials north of Yi Province city, and together with Jiong ascended the altar, drank blood, and established a covenant, surrendering the city to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then led the civil and military officials to the north of Yi Province city, where he and Jiong ascended the altar, swore a blood oath, and surrendered the city to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝元年，授侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，封歸善縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was appointed Palace Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and Director with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed as Duke of Guishan with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was made Palace Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and Director with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, and created Duke of Guishan with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進爵黃臺郡公，增邑一千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, his noble rank was advanced to Duke of Huangtai and his fief increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin came to the throne, Hui was advanced to Duke of Huangtai and his fief was increased by one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 武成中，世宗令諸文儒於麟趾殿校定經史，仍撰《世譜》，撝亦預焉。

translations.literal: During the Wucheng era, Emperor Shizong ordered the literary scholars to collate the classics and histories at Qilin Hall and also to compile the Genealogies of the Age; Hui also took part.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wucheng era, Emperor Shizong had the literary scholars collate the classics and histories in Qilin Hall and compile the Genealogies of the Age; Hui took part in this work.

sentences.zh: 尋以母老，兼有疾疹，五日番上，便隔晨昏，請在外著書。

translations.literal: Soon, because his mother was elderly and he himself also suffered from illness, attending court on a five-day rotation kept him from morning and evening attendance upon her, and he requested permission to write at home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, with an aged mother at home and illness of his own, the five-day court rotation kept him from seeing her morning and evening, and he asked leave to write at home.

sentences.zh: 有詔許焉。

translations.literal: An imperial edict granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his request.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，授禮部中大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding he was appointed Grand Master of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoding he was appointed Grand Master of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 又以撝有歸款之功，別賜食多陵縣五百戶，收其租賦。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Hui had the merit of coming over in allegiance, he was separately granted the income of five hundred households in Duoling County to collect its rents and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his merit in surrendering in good faith, he was also granted the tax income of five hundred households in Duoling County.

sentences.zh: 三年，出為上州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year he went out as Governor of Shang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was sent out as governor of Shang Province.

sentences.zh: 為政仁恕，以禮讓為本。

translations.literal: In government he was benevolent and forgiving, taking courtesy and deference as his foundation.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was humane and forgiving, grounded in courtesy and deference.

sentences.zh: 嘗至元日，獄中所有囚繫，悉放歸家，聽三日，然後赴獄。

translations.literal: Once, on New Year's Day, he released all prisoners held in the jail to return home, allowing them three days before they were to report back to prison.
translations.idiomatic: On one New Year's Day he released every prisoner in the jail to go home for three days, after which they were to return.

sentences.zh: 主者固執不可。

translations.literal: The officials in charge firmly objected that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The officials in charge firmly insisted that this could not be done.

sentences.zh: 撝曰：「昔王長、虞延見稱前史，吾雖寡德，竊懷景行。

translations.literal: Hui said: "In former ages Wang Chang and Yu Yan were praised in the histories; though I lack their virtue, I privately cherish their lofty example.
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "Wang Chang and Yu Yan were praised in the histories of old; though I lack their virtue, I still aspire to follow their example.

sentences.zh: 導民以信，方自此始。

translations.literal: To lead the people by trust—let it begin here.
translations.idiomatic: To lead the people by trust—that must begin here.

sentences.zh: 以之獲罪，彌所甘心，幸勿慮也。

translations.literal: If I am punished for this, I am all the more willing; please do not worry.
translations.idiomatic: If I am punished for it, I will accept that gladly; please do not worry on my account.

sentences.zh: 」諸囚荷恩，竝依限而至。

translations.literal: "All the prisoners, grateful for his kindness, returned together within the allotted time.
translations.idiomatic: "Every prisoner, grateful for his kindness, returned within the allotted time.

sentences.zh: 吏民稱其惠化。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners praised his benevolent governance.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike praised his benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 秩滿當還，部民李漆等三百餘人上表，乞更留兩載。

translations.literal: When his term was complete and he was due to return, more than three hundred local people led by Li Qi submitted a memorial asking that he be kept two years longer.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and he was due to return to court, more than three hundred local people led by Li Qi petitioned that he be kept for two more years.

sentences.zh: 詔雖弗許，甚嘉美之。

translations.literal: Although the edict did not grant this, the court greatly commended the sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not grant the request, but greatly praised the gesture.

sentences.zh: 及撝入朝，屬置露門學。

translations.literal: When Hui came to court, it happened that the Lumen Gate Academy was being established.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui came to court, the Lumen Gate Academy was being established.

sentences.zh: 高祖以撝與唐瑾、元偉、王褒等四人俱為文學博士。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu appointed Hui together with Tang Jin, Yuan Wei, and Wang Bao, four men in all, as Literary Doctors.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu appointed Hui, together with Tang Jin, Yuan Wei, and Wang Bao, as Literary Doctors.

sentences.zh: 撝以母老，表請歸養私門，曰：「臣聞出忠入孝，理深人紀；

translations.literal: Hui, because his mother was elderly, submitted a memorial requesting to return home to support her, saying: "Your servant has heard that going forth in loyalty and returning in filial piety is a principle deeply rooted in human relations;
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was elderly, Hui submitted a memorial asking to return home to care for her, saying, "I have heard that going forth in loyalty and returning in filial piety lies at the heart of human conduct;

sentences.zh: 昏定晨省，事切天經。

translations.literal: attending her at evening and inquiring after her in the morning is a matter bound to Heaven's constant way.
translations.idiomatic: to comfort her at night and greet her in the morning is a duty ordained by Heaven itself.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下握鎮臨朝，垂衣禦宇，孝治天下，仁覃草木。

translations.literal: I bow before Your Majesty, who holds the reins and faces the court, rules the realm with folded robes, governs the world through filial piety, and extends benevolence even to grass and trees.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty holds the realm in steady hands, rules with effortless grace, governs the world through filial piety, and extends kindness even to grass and trees.

sentences.zh: 是以微臣冒陳至願。

translations.literal: Therefore your humble servant ventures to state his utmost wish.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I dare lay my deepest wish before you.

sentences.zh: 臣母妾褚年過養禮，乞解今職，侍奉私庭。

translations.literal: My mother, the lady Chu, has passed the age at which she should be supported; I beg to be relieved of my present office and to serve her in our private household.
translations.idiomatic: My mother, Lady Chu, has reached the age when she should be supported in her home; I beg to be released from my present post so that I may attend her there.

sentences.zh: 伏願天慈，特垂矜許。

translations.literal: I bow in hope that Heaven's compassion may especially grant its pity and approval.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that your heavenly kindness will grant this request.

sentences.zh: 臣披款歸朝，十有六載，恩深海岳，報淺涓埃。

translations.literal: Your servant has offered his loyalty and returned to court for sixteen years; the grace shown him is deep as sea and mountain, while his repayment is slight as a speck of dust.
translations.idiomatic: For sixteen years I have served the court in good faith; your grace to me is deep as the sea and high as the mountains, while my repayment has been no more than a speck of dust.

sentences.zh: 肆師掌禮，竟無稱職；

translations.literal: As Director of the Four Departments in charge of ritual, I proved unfit for the post;
translations.idiomatic: As master of ceremonies in charge of ritual, I proved unfit for the post;

sentences.zh: 淅隈督察，空妨能官。

translations.literal: as inspector on the Xi frontier, I merely obstructed capable officials.
translations.idiomatic: and as inspector on the Xi frontier I only stood in the way of men who could have served better.

sentences.zh: 方辭違闕庭，屏迹閭里，低佪係慕，戀悚兼深。

translations.literal: Now, as I take leave of the imperial court and withdraw to my neighborhood, I linger in longing and my attachment and apprehension are alike profound.
translations.idiomatic: As I now leave the imperial court and withdraw to my home, I linger in longing, torn between devotion and dread.

sentences.zh: 」高祖未許，詔曰：「開府梁之宗英，今則任等三事。

translations.literal: "Emperor Gaozu did not grant this and issued an edict saying: "The Director, a leading luminary of Liang, now holds a post equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor refused. His edict read, "The Director is a leading luminary of Liang and now holds rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 所謂楚雖有材，周實用之。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by saying that though Chu has talent, Zhou is the one that puts it to use.
translations.idiomatic: It is the old saying: Chu may have the talent, but Zhou is the state that puts it to use.

sentences.zh: 方藉謀猷，匡朕不逮。

translations.literal: I am just now relying on your counsel to correct my shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: I am counting on your counsel to remedy my failings.

sentences.zh: 然進思盡忠，退安侍養者，義在公私兼濟。

translations.literal: Yet advancing to think of utmost loyalty and withdrawing to attend one's parents in peace—the meaning lies in harmonizing public and private duty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the man who serves loyally at court and peacefully supports his parents at home embodies the balance of public and private duty.

sentences.zh: 豈容全欲狥己，虧此至公，乖所望也。

translations.literal: How can I allow you wholly to indulge yourself and impair this supreme public good? That would fall short of what I expect.
translations.idiomatic: How could I let you indulge yourself entirely at the expense of the public good? That is not what I expect of you.

sentences.zh: 」尋以母憂去職。

translations.literal: "Soon afterward he left office on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: "Soon afterward he left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 撝善草隸，名亞於王褒。

translations.literal: Hui was skilled in cursive and clerical script; his reputation was second only to Wang Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Hui excelled in cursive and clerical script and was ranked just below Wang Bao.

sentences.zh: 算數醫方，咸亦留意。

translations.literal: He also took note of arithmetic and medical prescriptions.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave attention to arithmetic and medicine.

sentences.zh: 所著詩賦雜文數萬言，頗行於世。

translations.literal: The poems, rhapsodies, and miscellaneous writings he composed number in the tens of thousands of words and circulated widely in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His poems, rhapsodies, and miscellaneous writings run to tens of thousands of words and circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 子濟嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ji succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 濟字德成，少仁厚，頗好屬文。

translations.literal: Ji, courtesy name Decheng, was benevolent and generous from youth and quite fond of literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, whose courtesy name was Decheng, was gentle and generous from youth and fond of writing.

sentences.zh: 蕭紀承制，授貞威將軍、蜀郡太守，遷東中郎將。

translations.literal: Xiao Ji, acting under an imperial commission, appointed him Loyal Martial General and Administrator of Shu Commandery, then promoted him to General of the East Center.
translations.idiomatic: Acting under imperial authority, Xiao Ji appointed him Loyal Martial General and administrator of Shu Commandery, then promoted him to General of the East Center.

sentences.zh: 從紀東下。

translations.literal: He followed Ji eastward.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Ji on the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 至巴東，聞迥圍成都，紀命濟率所部赴援。

translations.literal: When they reached Badong and heard that Jiong was besieging Chengdu, Ji ordered Ji to lead his command to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: At Badong they learned that Jiong was besieging Chengdu, and Ji ordered his son to lead their forces to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 比至，撝已降。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, Hui had already surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived, Hui had already surrendered.

sentences.zh: 仍從撝入朝。

translations.literal: He then followed Hui to court.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Hui to the Zhou court.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，除中外府記室參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he was appointed Recorder in the Secretariat of the Palace and Capital Offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin came to the throne, he was appointed recorder in the secretariat of the palace and capital offices.

sentences.zh: 後至蒲陽郡守、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Later he rose to Administrator of Puyang, Grand General of the Chariots and Cavalry, and Director with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He later became administrator of Puyang, Grand General of the Chariots and Cavalry, and Director with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 蕭世怡，梁武帝弟鄱陽王恢之子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Shiyi was a son of Prince Poyang Hui, younger brother of Emperor Wu of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Shiyi was the son of Prince Poyang Hui, a younger brother of Emperor Wu of Liang.

sentences.zh: 以名犯太祖諱，故稱字焉。

translations.literal: Because his personal name violated the taboo on the Grand Patriarch's name, he is referred to by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Because his personal name violated the taboo on the Grand Patriarch's name, the text refers to him by his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 幼而聰慧，頗涉經史。

translations.literal: From childhood he was clever and had read considerably in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from childhood, he had read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 梁大同元年，封豐城縣侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong of Liang he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fengcheng with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong of Liang he was created Marquis of Fengcheng with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 除給事中，轉太子洗馬。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant Within the Gates, then transferred to Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant Within the Gates and later became Groom of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋入直殿省，轉太子中舍人。

translations.literal: Soon he entered service in the Palace Attendance Office and was transferred to Palace Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered the Palace Attendance Office and was later made Palace Attendant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 出為持節、仁威將軍、譙州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff, Benevolent Martial General, and Governor of Qiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital as Bearer of the Staff, Benevolent Martial General, and governor of Qiao Province.

sentences.zh: 及侯景為亂，路由城下，襲而陷之，世怡遂被執。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, his route passed below the city wall; he attacked and took it, and Shiyi was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, his army passed below the city, stormed it, and took Shiyi prisoner.

sentences.zh: 尋遁逃得免，至于江陵。

translations.literal: Soon he escaped and made his way to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He soon escaped and fled to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝承制授侍中。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang, acting under an imperial commission, appointed him Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang, exercising imperial authority, appointed him Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 及平侯景，以世怡為兼太宰、太常卿，與中衛長史樂子雲拜謁山陵。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Shiyi was appointed concurrent Grand Mentor and Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and together with Chief Clerk of the Central Guard Yue Ziyun he paid homage at the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was defeated, Shiyi was made concurrent Grand Mentor and Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and, together with Chief Clerk of the Central Guard Yue Ziyun, performed the rites at the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 承聖二年，授使持節、平西將軍、臨川內史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the West, and Interior Administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chengsheng he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the West, and interior administrator of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 旣以陸納據湘川，道路擁塞，改授平南將軍、桂陽內史。

translations.literal: Because Lu Na held Xiang River and the roads were blocked, his appointment was changed to General Who Pacifies the South and Interior Administrator of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Because Lu Na held the Xiang region and the roads were blocked, his appointment was changed to General Who Pacifies the South and interior administrator of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 未至郡，屬於謹平江陵，遂隨兄修在郢州。

translations.literal: Before he reached his commandery, it happened that Yuwen Jiong pacified Jiangling, and he therefore followed his elder brother Xiu at Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached his post, Yuwen Jiong captured Jiangling, and he joined his elder brother Xiu at Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 及修卒，卽以世怡為刺史。

translations.literal: When Xiu died, Shiyi was immediately made governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu died, Shiyi was immediately appointed governor in his place.

sentences.zh: 湘州刺史王琳率舟師襲世怡，世怡以州輸琳。

translations.literal: Wang Lin, Governor of Xiang Province, led a fleet to attack Shiyi, and Shiyi surrendered the province to Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin, governor of Xiang Province, led a fleet against him, and Shiyi surrendered the province to Lin.

sentences.zh: 時陳武帝執政，徵為侍中。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wu of Chen held power and summoned him to serve as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chen Wudi held power and summoned him to serve as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 世怡疑而不就，乃奔于齊。

translations.literal: Shiyi was suspicious and did not go; he fled instead to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi was wary and refused; he fled to Northern Qi instead.

sentences.zh: 除車騎大將軍、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Qi appointed him Grand General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尋出為永州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，晉公護東伐，大將軍權景宣略地河南。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding, Duke Jin of Jin Hu launched an eastern campaign, and the Grand General Quan Jingxuan reduced the lands south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Baoding, Duke Jin Hu launched an eastern campaign, and the Grand General Quan Jingxuan advanced into the lands south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 世怡聞豫州刺史王士良已降，遂來歸款。

translations.literal: When Shiyi heard that Wang Shiliang, Governor of Yu Province, had already surrendered, he came over in allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Wang Shiliang, governor of Yu Province, had already surrendered, Shiyi came over to Zhou in turn.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，封義興郡公，邑一千三百戶。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and Director with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yixing with a fief of one thousand three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and Director with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, and created Duke of Yixing with a fief of thirteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，授蔡州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe he was appointed Governor of Cai Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianhe he was appointed governor of Cai Province.

sentences.zh: 政存簡惠，不尚苛察，深為吏民所安。

translations.literal: His government was marked by simplicity and kindness; he did not esteem harsh scrutiny, and officials and commoners were deeply reassured by him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was simple and humane; he did not favor harsh scrutiny, and officials and commoners alike found security under him.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒於州。

translations.literal: In the third year he died in his province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈本官、加幷洛永三州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted his former offices and additionally made Governor of the three provinces of Bing, Luo, and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted his former offices and additionally invested as governor of Bing, Luo, and Yong provinces.

sentences.zh: 子子寶嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zibao succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zibao inherited his title and position.

sentences.zh: 子寶美風儀，善談笑，年未弱冠，名重一時。

translations.literal: Zibao had a fine bearing and was skilled in conversation and wit; before he had reached twenty, his name carried great weight for a time.
translations.idiomatic: Zibao had an elegant presence and a gift for conversation and wit; before he was even twenty, his reputation stood high in his day.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝輔政，引為丞相府典簽，深被識遇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui served as regent, he summoned him to serve as Chief Clerk in the Chancellor's Office, and he was deeply recognized and favored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was regent, he brought Zibao into the chancellor's office as chief clerk and treated him with marked favor.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，官至吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: During the Kaihuang era he rose to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang reign he rose to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 後坐事被誅。

translations.literal: Later he was executed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was later executed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 蕭圓肅字明恭，梁武帝之孫，武陵王紀之子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Yuansu, courtesy name Minggong, was a grandson of Emperor Wu of Liang and a son of Prince of Wuling Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yuansu, whose courtesy name was Minggong, was a grandson of Emperor Wu of Liang and the son of Prince of Wuling Ji.

sentences.zh: 風度淹雅，敏而好學。

translations.literal: His bearing was refined and elegant, and he was quick-witted and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Refined and graceful in bearing, he was quick of mind and devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 紀稱尊號，封宜都郡王，邑三千戶，除侍中、寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: When Ji assumed an imperial title, Yuansu was enfeoffed as Prince of Yidu with a fief of three thousand households and appointed Palace Attendant and General of Distant Pacification.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji declared himself emperor, Yuansu was created Prince of Yidu with a fief of three thousand households and appointed Palace Attendant and General of Distant Pacification.

sentences.zh: 紀率兵下峽，令蕭撝守成都，以圓肅為之副。

translations.literal: Ji led troops down through the gorges, ordered Xiao Hui to hold Chengdu, and made Yuansu his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Ji marched his army down through the gorges, left Xiao Hui to hold Chengdu, and appointed Yuansu as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 及尉遲迥至，圓肅與撝俱降。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Jiong arrived, Yuansu and Hui both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Jiong arrived, Yuansu and Hui surrendered together.

sentences.zh: 授驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、侍中，封安化縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Director with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies, and Palace Attendant, and enfeoffed as Duke of Anhua with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Director with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, and Palace Attendant, and created Duke of Anhua with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，進封棘城郡公，增邑一千戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, he was advanced to Duke of Jicheng with an additional one thousand households added to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizong's reign he was promoted to Duke of Jicheng, with one thousand households added to his fief.

sentences.zh: 以圓肅有歸款之勳，別賜食思君縣五百戶，收其租賦。

translations.literal: Because Yuansu had merit in coming over in allegiance, he was separately granted the income of five hundred households from Sijun County, and its rents and taxes were collected for him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yuansu had merit in surrendering and submitting, he was separately granted the revenues of five hundred households in Sijun County.

sentences.zh: 保定三年，除畿伯中大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding he was appointed Grand Master of the Jibo.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoding he was appointed Grand Master of the Jibo.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜咸陽郡守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Administrator of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed administrator of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 圓肅寬猛相濟，甚有政績。

translations.literal: Yuansu combined leniency and severity, and his administrative achievements were considerable.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu balanced leniency with firmness and achieved notable success in office.

sentences.zh: 天和四年，遷陵州刺史，尋詔令隨衛國公直鎮襄陽，遂不之部。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianhe he was transferred to Governor of Ling Province; soon he was ordered by edict to follow Duke of Weiguo Yu Zhi in garrisoning Xiangyang, and therefore did not go to his province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianhe he was transferred to governor of Ling Province, but soon received orders to accompany Duke of Weiguo Yu Zhi in garrisoning Xiangyang and never took up his provincial post.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，授太子少傅，增邑九百戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiande he was appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, with nine hundred households added to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande he was appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, with nine hundred households added to his fief.

sentences.zh: 圓肅以任當師傅，調護是職。

translations.literal: Yuansu, considering that his duty lay in serving as tutor, regarded nurturing and protection as his office.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu, knowing his duty as tutor lay in guidance and care, took that responsibility as his charge.

sentences.zh: 乃作《少傅箴》曰：

translations.literal: He therefore composed the 《Admonition of the Junior Tutor》, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He therefore composed the 《Admonition of the Junior Tutor》, which reads:

sentences.zh: 惟王建國，辨方正位。

translations.literal: When a king establishes a state, he determines the directions and fixes the positions.
translations.idiomatic: When a king founds a state, he sets the cardinal directions and fixes the positions of all things.

sentences.zh: 左史記言，右史記事。

translations.literal: The left scribe records words; the right scribe records affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The scribe on the left records speech; the scribe on the right records events.

sentences.zh: 莫不援立太子，為皇之貳。

translations.literal: None fail to install the crown prince as the emperor's second.
translations.idiomatic: In every case a crown prince is installed to serve as the emperor's second.

sentences.zh: 是以《易》稱明兩，《禮》云上嗣。

translations.literal: Therefore the 《Book of Changes》 speaks of "bright twofold," and the 《Book of Rites》 speaks of "the heir above."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the 《Book of Changes》 speaks of "bright twofold," and the 《Book of Rites》 speaks of "the heir above."

sentences.zh: 東序養德，震方主器。

translations.literal: In the eastern school one cultivates virtue; in the quarter of Zhen one holds the vessel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eastern school he cultivates virtue; in the quarter of Zhen he holds the sacred vessel.

sentences.zh: 束發就學，《宵雅》更肄。

translations.literal: With hair bound, he begins study and further pursues the 《Xiaoya》.
translations.idiomatic: With hair bound he begins his studies and goes on to master the 《Xiaoya》.

sentences.zh: 朝讀百篇，乙夜乃寐。

translations.literal: By day he reads a hundred texts; only at the second watch of night does he sleep.
translations.idiomatic: By day he reads a hundred texts; only in the second watch of the night does he sleep.

sentences.zh: 愛日惜力，寸陰無棄。

translations.literal: He cherishes the day and spares his strength; not a moment's shadow is wasted.
translations.idiomatic: He cherishes each day and husbands his strength, wasting not a single moment.

sentences.zh: 視膳再飯，寢門三至。

translations.literal: He inspects meals twice and goes to the bedchamber door thrice.
translations.idiomatic: He attends to his parent's meals twice daily and comes to the bedchamber door three times.

sentences.zh: 小心翼翼，大孝蒸蒸。

translations.literal: With utmost caution and care, great filial piety ever rises.
translations.idiomatic: With utmost caution and care, his great filial devotion ever ascends.

sentences.zh: 謀謨計慮，問對疑丞。

translations.literal: He plans counsels and schemes, questioning and answering as an assistant to resolve doubts.
translations.idiomatic: He deliberates on counsel and strategy, questioning and answering to resolve doubts as the crown prince's aide.

sentences.zh: 安樂必敬，無忘戰兢。

translations.literal: In ease and joy one must be reverent; never forget fear and caution.
translations.idiomatic: Even in ease and pleasure one must remain reverent; never forget fear and vigilance.

sentences.zh: 夫天道益謙，人道惡盈。

translations.literal: Heaven's way increases the humble; the way of man abhors fullness.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's way rewards humility; the way of man abhors excess.

sentences.zh: 漢嗣不絕乎馳道，魏儲回環於鄴城。

translations.literal: The heir of Han was not cut off at the imperial road; the crown prince of Wei circled about at Yecheng.
translations.idiomatic: The heir of Han was not cut off along the imperial road; the crown prince of Wei was driven back and forth at Yecheng.

sentences.zh: 前史攸載，後世揚名。

translations.literal: Former histories record these things, and later ages proclaim their names.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier histories record these examples, and later ages proclaim their fame.

sentences.zh: 三善旣備，萬國以貞。

translations.literal: When the three virtues are complete, the myriad states are thereby made steadfast.
translations.idiomatic: When the three virtues are complete, the myriad states stand firm in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 姬周長久，實賴元良。

translations.literal: Zhou of Ji endured long, truly relying on the worthy heir.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou of the House of Ji endured long, truly through reliance on a worthy heir.

sentences.zh: 嬴秦短祚，誠由少陽。

translations.literal: Qin of Ying had a brief reign, truly because of the young yang heir.
translations.idiomatic: Qin of the House of Ying had a brief reign, truly because of an unworthy young heir.

sentences.zh: 雖卜年七百，有德過歷而昌；

translations.literal: Although one may divine a span of seven hundred years, with virtue one surpasses the allotted years and flourishes;
translations.idiomatic: Though one may read seven hundred years in the oracle, with virtue one exceeds the allotted span and prospers;

sentences.zh: 數世［一］萬

translations.literal: for generations, with the character 'one' emended, myriad
translations.idiomatic: for generation after generation without end

translations.literal: (one)
translations.idiomatic: (textual emendation: one)

sentences.zh: ，無德不及而亡。

translations.literal: , without virtue one does not reach it and perishes.
translations.idiomatic: , without virtue one does not attain it and perishes.

sentences.zh: 敬之敬之，天惟顯思。

translations.literal: Be reverent, be reverent; heaven alone considers and knows.
translations.idiomatic: Be reverent, be reverent—heaven alone sees and considers.

sentences.zh: 光副皇極，永固洪基。

translations.literal: May you shine as counterpart to the imperial apex and forever secure the great foundation.
translations.idiomatic: May you shine as the complement to the throne and forever secure the great foundation.

sentences.zh: 觀德審諭，授告職司。

translations.literal: Observe virtue, examine instruction, and transmit this admonition to those charged with office.
translations.idiomatic: Observe virtue, examine instruction, and convey this admonition to those who hold office.

sentences.zh: 太子見而悅之，致書勞問。

translations.literal: The crown prince read it and was pleased; he sent a letter expressing appreciation and inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince read it with delight and sent a letter of appreciation and inquiry.

sentences.zh: 六年，授豐州刺史，增邑通前三千七百戶。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Governor of Feng Province, with his fief increased in all to three thousand seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed governor of Feng Province, with his fief increased in all to thirty-seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋進位上開府儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Senior Director with the same privileges as a Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Senior Director with privileges equal to those of a Grand General.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，入為司宗中大夫，俄授洛州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng he entered the capital as Grand Master of the Directorate of the Imperial Clan; soon he was appointed Governor of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanzheng he entered the capital as Grand Master of the Directorate of the Imperial Clan and was soon appointed governor of Luo Province.

sentences.zh: 大象末，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daxiang era he was advanced to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang era he was promoted to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，授貝州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sui's Kaihuang era he was appointed Governor of Bei Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era of Sui he was appointed governor of Bei Province.

sentences.zh: 以母老請歸就養，隋文帝許之。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old, he requested to return home to support her, and Emperor Wen of Sui granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was elderly, he asked to return home to care for her, and Emperor Wen of Sui granted his request.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，時年四十六。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, at the age of forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died, at the age of forty-six.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷，又撰時人詩筆為《文海》四十卷，《廣堪》十卷，《淮海亂離志》四卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collected writings in ten scrolls, and also compiled contemporary poetry and prose into the 《Literary Sea》 in forty scrolls, the 《Broad Mirror》 in ten scrolls, and the 《Record of Turmoil and Separation in the Huai-Hai Region》 in four scrolls, all of which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected writings in ten scrolls, and also compiled contemporary poetry and prose into the 《Literary Sea》 in forty scrolls, the 《Broad Mirror》 in ten scrolls, and the 《Record of Turmoil and Separation in the Huai-Hai Region》 in four scrolls, all of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 時梁元帝旣有克復之功，而大圜兄汝南王大封等猶未通謁。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Yuan of Liang already had the merit of recovery, yet Dahuan's elder brother, Prince of Runan Dafeng, and others had still not come to pay their respects.
translations.idiomatic: By then Emperor Yuan of Liang had already achieved the recovery of the realm, yet Dahuan's elder brother Prince of Runan Dafeng and others had still not come to pay their respects.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝性旣忌刻，甚恨望之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang was by nature jealous and harsh, and he greatly resented and looked askance at this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang was jealous and harsh by nature, and he deeply resented their absence.

sentences.zh: 乃謂大圜曰：「汝兩兄久不出，汝可以意召之。

translations.literal: He therefore said to Dahuan, "Your two elder brothers have long stayed away; you may summon them as you see fit.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore said to Dahuan, "Your two elder brothers have long stayed away; you may summon them as you think best.

sentences.zh: 」大圜卽日曉諭兩兄，相繼出謁，元帝乃安之。

translations.literal: " That same day Dahuan explained the matter to his two elder brothers, and they came out in succession to pay their respects; Emperor Yuan was then reassured.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day Dahuan explained the matter to his two elder brothers, and they came out in turn to pay their respects; Emperor Yuan was then reassured.

sentences.zh: 大圜以世多故，恐讒愬生焉，乃屏絕人事。

translations.literal: Dahuan, because the age was full of troubles, feared that slander and accusations might arise, and therefore cut himself off from worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Because the times were turbulent, Dahuan feared slander and accusation and withdrew from worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 門客左右不過三兩人，不妄遊狎。

translations.literal: His retainers and attendants numbered no more than two or three, and he did not casually go about in frivolous company.
translations.idiomatic: He kept no more than two or three retainers and attendants and did not casually go about in frivolous company.

sentences.zh: 兄姊之間，止箋疏而已。

translations.literal: With his elder brothers and elder sisters he communicated only by letter.
translations.idiomatic: With his elder brothers and sisters he communicated only by letter.

sentences.zh: 恒以讀《詩》、《禮》、《書》、《易》為事。

translations.literal: He constantly made reading the 《Book of Songs》, the 《Book of Rites》, the 《Book of Documents》, and the 《Book of Changes》 his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself constantly to reading the 《Book of Songs》, the 《Book of Rites》, the 《Book of Documents》, and the 《Book of Changes》.

sentences.zh: 元帝嘗自問《五經》要事數十條，大圜辭約指明，應答無滯。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan once personally questioned him on several dozen essential points from the 《Five Classics》; Dahuan's words were concise yet pointed, and his replies were without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan once personally questioned him on several dozen essential points from the 《Five Classics》; Dahuan answered concisely and clearly, without the least hesitation.

sentences.zh: 元帝甚歎美之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan greatly sighed in admiration of him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan greatly admired him.

sentences.zh: 因曰：「昔河間好學，爾旣有之，臨淄好文，爾亦兼之。

translations.literal: He then said, "In former times the Prince of Hejian loved learning—you already have that; Linzi loved literature—you also combine that.
translations.idiomatic: He then said, "In former times the Prince of Hejian loved learning—you already have that; Linzi loved literature—you combine that as well.

sentences.zh: 然有東平為善，彌高前載，吾重之愛之，爾當效焉。

translations.literal: Yet there was also the Prince of Dongping, who excelled in goodness and stands even higher in the records of old; I esteem and love that, and you should emulate it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet there was also the Prince of Dongping, who excelled in goodness and stands even higher in the records of old; I esteem and love that example, and you should follow it.

sentences.zh: 」及於謹軍至，元帝乃令大封充使請和，大圜副焉，其實質也。

translations.literal: " When Yuwen Jiong's army arrived, Emperor Yuan ordered Dafeng to serve as envoy to sue for peace, with Dahuan as his deputy—in truth he was a hostage.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yuwen Jiong's army arrived, Emperor Yuan ordered Dafeng to serve as envoy to sue for peace, with Dahuan as his deputy—in truth a hostage.

sentences.zh: 出至軍所，信宿，元帝降。

translations.literal: They went out to the army camp; after two nights Emperor Yuan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: They went out to the army camp, and after two nights Emperor Yuan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，客長安，太祖以客禮待之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was a guest at Chang'an, and the Grand Preceptor treated him with the rites due a guest.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei he lived as a guest at Chang'an, and the Grand Preceptor treated him with the courtesy due a guest.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，詔曰：「梁汝南王蕭大封、晉熙王蕭大圜等，梁國子孫，宜存優禮，式遺茅土，寔允舊章。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding an edict said, "Xiao Dafeng, Prince of Runan of Liang, Xiao Dahuan, Prince of Jinxi of Liang, and others, as descendants of the Liang state, should receive honored treatment; to grant them fiefs accords with the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoding an edict said, "Xiao Dafeng, Prince of Runan of Liang, Xiao Dahuan, Prince of Jinxi of Liang, and others, as descendants of the Liang house, should receive honored treatment; to grant them fiefs accords with established precedent.

sentences.zh: 大封可封晉陵縣公，大圜封始寧縣公，邑各一千戶。

translations.literal: Dafeng may be enfeoffed as Duke of Jinling, and Dahuan as Duke of Shining, each with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Dafeng is to be created Duke of Jinling, and Dahuan Duke of Shining, each with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 」尋加大圜車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: " Soon Dahuan was additionally made Grand General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Director with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: " Dahuan was soon additionally appointed Grand General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Director with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 幷賜田宅、奴婢、牛馬、粟帛等。

translations.literal: He was also granted fields and dwellings, male and female servants, cattle and horses, grain and cloth, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted fields and dwellings, servants, cattle and horses, grain and cloth, and the like.

sentences.zh: 俄而開麟趾殿，招集學士。

translations.literal: Soon the Linzhi Hall was opened and scholars were gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Linzhi Hall was opened and scholars were gathered there.

sentences.zh: 大圜預焉。

translations.literal: Dahuan participated in it.
translations.idiomatic: Dahuan was among them.

sentences.zh: 《梁武帝集》四十卷，《簡文集》九十卷，各止一本，江陵平後，竝藏秘閤。

translations.literal: The 《Collected Works of Emperor Wu of Liang》 in forty scrolls and the 《Collected Works of Emperor Jian》 in ninety scrolls, each existing in only one copy, after the pacification of Jiangling were both stored in the secret archive.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Collected Works of Emperor Wu of Liang》 in forty scrolls and the 《Collected Works of Emperor Jian》 in ninety scrolls, each existing in only one copy, were both stored in the secret archive after the fall of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 大圜旣入麟趾，方得見之。

translations.literal: Only after Dahuan entered the Linzhi Hall was he able to see them.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Dahuan entered the Linzhi Hall was he able to see them.

sentences.zh: 乃手寫二集，一年竝畢。

translations.literal: He then copied both collections by hand and finished both within one year.
translations.idiomatic: He then copied both collections by hand and finished them within a single year.

sentences.zh: 識者稱歎之。

translations.literal: Those who knew praised and marveled at this.
translations.idiomatic: Those who knew of it praised and marveled at the feat.

sentences.zh: 大圜深信因果，心安閒放。

translations.literal: Dahuan deeply believed in cause and effect, and his mind was at ease in leisure and release.
translations.idiomatic: Dahuan deeply believed in karma, and his mind was at ease in a life of leisure.

sentences.zh: 嘗言之曰：

translations.literal: He once spoke of it, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He once said:

sentences.zh: 拂衣褰裳，無吞舟之漏網；

translations.literal: Shaking out one's robes and lifting one's skirts, one escapes the net that lets no great fish through;
translations.idiomatic: Shaking out one's robes and lifting one's skirts, one escapes the net that lets no great fish slip through;

sentences.zh: 掛冠懸節，慮我志之未從。

translations.literal: hanging up one's cap and suspending one's insignia, one fears that one's resolve has not yet been fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: hanging up one's cap and laying aside one's insignia, one still fears one's resolve has not yet been fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 儻獲展禽之免，有美慈明之進。

translations.literal: If one could obtain exemption like Zhan Qin, there would be the fine advance of Ciming.
translations.idiomatic: If one could obtain release like Zhan Qin, there would be the fine example of Ciming's withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 如蒙北叟之放，實勝濟南之征。

translations.literal: If one were granted release like the old man of the north, it would truly surpass the campaign against Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: If one were granted freedom like the old man of the north, it would truly be better than the campaign against Jinan.

sentences.zh: 其故何哉？

translations.literal: What is the reason for this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 夫閭閻者有優遊之美，朝廷者有簪佩之累，蓋由來久矣。

translations.literal: In the lanes and wards there is the beauty of ease and leisure; at court there is the burden of official insignia—this has been so from long ago.
translations.idiomatic: Life in the lanes and wards holds the beauty of ease and leisure; life at court carries the burden of rank and office—this has been so since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 留侯追蹤于松子，陶朱成術于辛文，良有以焉。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Liu followed in the tracks of Master Songzi; Tao Zhu perfected his art with Xin Wen—there is good reason for this.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Liu followed in the footsteps of Master Songzi; Tao Zhu perfected his art with Xin Wen—there is good reason in that.

sentences.zh: 況乎智不逸羣，行不高物，而欲辛苦一生，何其僻也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when one's wisdom does not surpass the multitude and one's conduct does not rise above others, yet one wishes to toil through a whole lifetime—how eccentric that is.
translations.idiomatic: When one's wisdom does not surpass the crowd and one's conduct does not rise above others, yet one wishes to toil through an entire lifetime—how eccentric that is.

sentences.zh: 豈如知足知止，蕭然無累。

translations.literal: How much better to know sufficiency and know when to stop, detached and without encumbrance.
translations.idiomatic: How much better to know when one has enough and when to stop, living detached and free of burden.

sentences.zh: 北山之北，棄絕人間，南山之南，超踰世網。

translations.literal: North of the northern mountains, abandoning the human world; south of the southern mountains, transcending the net of worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: North of the northern mountains, leaving the human world behind; south of the southern mountains, transcending the snares of worldly life.

sentences.zh: 面修原而帶流水，倚郊甸而枕平皋，築蝸舍於叢林，構環堵於幽薄。

translations.literal: Facing broad plains and girded by flowing waters, leaning on suburban fields and resting on level heights, building a snail's dwelling amid dense groves and erecting a single ring of walls in a secluded thicket.
translations.idiomatic: Facing broad plains girded by flowing waters, resting on suburban fields and level heights, building a humble dwelling amid dense groves and erecting a single ring of walls in a secluded thicket.

sentences.zh: 近瞻煙霧，遠睇風雲。

translations.literal: Looking near upon mist and smoke, gazing far upon wind and clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Looking near upon mist and smoke, gazing far upon wind and clouds.

sentences.zh: 藉纖草以蔭長松，結幽蘭而援芳桂。

translations.literal: Using slender grass to shade tall pines, binding orchids and supporting fragrant cassia.
translations.idiomatic: Using slender grasses to shade tall pines, planting orchids and supporting fragrant cassia.

sentences.zh: 仰翔禽於百仞，俯泳鱗於千潯。

translations.literal: Looking up at soaring birds a hundred ren above, looking down at swimming scales in a thousand fathoms of water.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up at soaring birds a hundred ren above, looking down at fish swimming in a thousand fathoms of water.

sentences.zh: 果園在後，開窗以臨花卉；

translations.literal: An orchard lies behind, and opening a window one overlooks flowers and plants;
translations.idiomatic: An orchard lies behind, and opening a window one overlooks flowers and plants;

sentences.zh: 蔬圃居前，坐簷而看灌甽。

translations.literal: a vegetable garden lies before, and sitting under the eaves one watches irrigation ditches.
translations.idiomatic: a vegetable garden lies in front, and sitting under the eaves one watches the irrigation ditches.

sentences.zh: 二頃以供饘粥，十畝以給絲麻。

translations.literal: Two qing supply gruel and porridge; ten mu provide silk and hemp.
translations.idiomatic: Two qing of land supply gruel and porridge; ten mu provide silk and hemp.

sentences.zh: 侍兒五三，可充紝織；

translations.literal: Five or three serving girls can suffice for spinning and weaving;
translations.idiomatic: Five or three serving girls can suffice for spinning and weaving;

sentences.zh: 家僮數四，足代耕耘。

translations.literal: Household slaves, several or four, suffice to take the place of plowing and hoeing.
translations.idiomatic: Four or so household servants suffice for the plowing and hoeing.

sentences.zh: 沽酪牧羊，協潘生之志；

translations.literal: Selling curds and tending sheep accords with Master Pan's aspiration;
translations.idiomatic: Selling curds and tending sheep fulfills the aspiration of Master Pan;

sentences.zh: 畜雞種黍，應莊叟之言。

translations.literal: Raising chickens and planting millet answers Old Man Zhuang's words.
translations.idiomatic: Raising chickens and planting millet answers the words of Old Master Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 獲菽尋泛氏之書，露葵征尹君之錄。

translations.literal: Harvesting beans and seeking Master Fan's writings; dew-covered mallow invokes Master Yin's records.
translations.idiomatic: Harvesting beans, one seeks Master Fan's agricultural writings; gathering dew-wet mallow, one invokes Master Yin's records.

sentences.zh: 烹羔豚而介春酒，迎伏臘而候歲時。

translations.literal: Cooking lamb and pork and presenting spring wine, welcoming the fu and la festivals and awaiting the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Cooking lamb and pork and serving them with spring wine, welcoming the fu and la festivals and marking the turn of the seasons.

sentences.zh: 披良書，探至賾，歌纂纂，唱烏烏，可以娛神，可以散慮。

translations.literal: Spreading fine books and probing the deepest principles, singing the 'cuancuan' ode and chanting 'wuwu,' one may delight the spirit and dispel cares.
translations.idiomatic: Opening fine books and probing their deepest teachings, singing the 'cuancuan' and chanting 'wuwu'—one may delight the spirit and scatter one's cares.

sentences.zh: 有朋自遠，揚搉古今。

translations.literal: When friends come from afar, one discusses and weighs past and present.
translations.idiomatic: When friends come from afar, one debates and weighs the past against the present.

sentences.zh: 田畯相過，劇談稼穡。

translations.literal: Field superintendents visit one another and earnestly discuss grain and crops.
translations.idiomatic: Field overseers call on one another and earnestly talk of planting and harvest.

sentences.zh: 斯亦足矣，樂不可支。

translations.literal: This too is sufficient; the joy cannot be borne.
translations.idiomatic: This alone is enough; the joy is beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 永保性命，何畏憂責。

translations.literal: Forever preserving life and fate, what fear of worry and blame?
translations.idiomatic: Preserving life forever, why fear worry or reproach?

sentences.zh: 豈若蹙足入絆，申脰就羈，遊帝王之門，趨宰衡之勢。

translations.literal: How much better than cramping one's feet to enter shackles, extending one's neck to accept bonds, roaming the gates of emperors and kings, and rushing after the power of prime ministers?
translations.idiomatic: How much better that than cramping one's feet to enter shackles, craning one's neck to accept bonds, roaming the courts of emperors and kings, and chasing after the power of prime ministers?

sentences.zh: 不知飄塵之少選，寧覺年祀之斯須。

translations.literal: Not knowing the brief moment of drifting dust, how could one feel the instant of passing years?
translations.idiomatic: Unaware that life is but a drifting speck for a brief moment, how could one sense that the years pass in an instant?

sentences.zh: 萬物營營，靡存其意，天道昧昧，安可問哉。

translations.literal: The myriad things bustle on, none preserving their intent; the Way of Heaven is obscure—how can it be questioned?
translations.idiomatic: The myriad things bustle without purpose; the Way of Heaven is obscure—how can one presume to question it?

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 人生若浮雲朝露，寧俟長繩系景，寔不願之。

translations.literal: Human life is like floating clouds and morning dew; how could one wait to tie the sun's shadow with a long rope—I truly do not wish for that.
translations.idiomatic: Human life is like floating clouds and morning dew; as for waiting to tie the sun's shadow with a long cord—that I truly do not wish for.

sentences.zh: 執燭夜遊，驚其迅邁。

translations.literal: Holding candles for night revels, one is startled by how swiftly it passes.
translations.idiomatic: Holding candles for night revels, one is startled by how swiftly time runs.

sentences.zh: 百年何幾，擎跽曲拳，四時如流，俛眉躡足。

translations.literal: How many years are there in a century? Raising hands, kneeling, bowing with bent fists; the four seasons flow like a stream; lowering brows and treading lightly.
translations.idiomatic: How few the years in a century—hands raised, knees bent, fists bowed in submission; the four seasons rush past like a stream; brows lowered, feet treading carefully.

sentences.zh: 出處無成，語默奚當。

translations.literal: Whether to serve or withdraw, no achievement; whether to speak or keep silent, what is fitting?
translations.idiomatic: To serve or withdraw achieves nothing; to speak or stay silent—what is fitting?

sentences.zh: 非直丘明所恥，抑亦宣尼恥之。

translations.literal: Not only would Qiu Ming be ashamed of this; Confucius too would be ashamed of it.
translations.idiomatic: Not only would Qiu Ming find this shameful—Confucius himself would be ashamed of it.

sentences.zh: 建德四年，除滕王逌友。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiande he was appointed companion to Prince of Teng, You.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiande he was appointed literary companion to Prince of Teng You.

sentences.zh: 逌嘗問大圜曰：「吾聞湘東王作《梁史》，有之乎？

translations.literal: You once asked Dahuan, saying, "I have heard that Prince of Xiangdong wrote the 《History of Liang》—is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Prince You once asked Dahuan, "I have heard that Prince of Xiangdong wrote the 《History of Liang》—is that so?

sentences.zh: 餘傳乃可抑揚，帝紀奚若？

translations.literal: The other biographies may allow praise and blame, but what of the imperial annals?
translations.idiomatic: Other biographies may be freely judged, but what of the imperial annals?

sentences.zh: 隱則非實，記則攘羊。

translations.literal: If concealed, it would not be factual; if recorded, it would be '[reporting] the stolen sheep.'
translations.idiomatic: To conceal would be untrue; to record would be [like reporting] the stolen sheep.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「言者之妄也。

translations.literal: He replied, "That is the speaker's wild talk.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "That is idle talk.

sentences.zh: 如使有之，亦不足怪。

translations.literal: If such a thing existed, it would not be strange either.
translations.idiomatic: Even if it existed, there would be nothing strange in that.

sentences.zh: 昔漢明為《世祖紀》，章帝為《顯宗紀》，殷鑒不遠，足為成例。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Ming of Han composed the 《Annals of Shizu》, and Emperor Zhang composed the 《Annals of Xianzong》; the mirror of recent precedent is not far off and suffices as an established case.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Han once composed the 《Annals of Shizu》, and Emperor Zhang the 《Annals of Xianzong》—recent precedent is close at hand and sufficient as established example.

sentences.zh: 且君子之過，如日月之蝕，彰于四海，安得而隱之？

translations.literal: Moreover, a gentleman's faults are like an eclipse of sun or moon, manifest to the four seas—how could they be concealed?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a gentleman's faults are like an eclipse of sun or moon, visible throughout the four seas—how could they be hidden?

sentences.zh: 如有不彰，亦安得而不隱？

translations.literal: If something is not manifest, how could one not conceal it?
translations.idiomatic: If something is not made manifest, how could one fail to conceal it?

sentences.zh: 蓋子為父隱，直在其中；

translations.literal: For the son conceals for the father, and uprightness lies therein;
translations.idiomatic: For a son may conceal a father's wrongdoing, and uprightness lies therein;

sentences.zh: 諱國之惡，抑又禮也。

translations.literal: concealing a state's disgrace is likewise ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: concealing the state's disgrace is likewise a matter of ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 」逌乃大笑。

translations.literal: " Prince You then laughed aloud.
translations.idiomatic: " Prince You then burst into loud laughter.

sentences.zh: 大圜性好學，務於著述。

translations.literal: Dahuan's nature was fond of learning, and he devoted himself to writing.
translations.idiomatic: Dahuan was devoted to learning and dedicated himself to authorship.

sentences.zh: 撰《梁舊事》三十卷，《寓記》三卷、《士喪儀注》五卷、《要決》兩卷，幷文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He compiled the 《Old Affairs of Liang》 in thirty scrolls, the 《Lodgings Record》 in three scrolls, the 《Commentary on the Rites for Scholars' Mourning》 in five scrolls, the 《Essential Decisions》 in two scrolls, and a collected writings in twenty scrolls altogether.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled the 《Old Affairs of Liang》 in thirty scrolls, the 《Lodgings Record》 in three scrolls, the 《Commentary on the Rites for Scholars' Mourning》 in five scrolls, the 《Essential Decisions》 in two scrolls, and a collected works of twenty scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 大封位至開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Dafeng reached the post of Director with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Dafeng rose to Director with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 大象末，為陳州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daxiang era he served as Governor of Chen Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang era he served as governor of Chen Province.

sentences.zh: 宗懍字元懍，南陽涅陽人也。

translations.literal: Zong Lin, courtesy name Yuanlin, was a man of Nielu in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Lin, whose courtesy name was Yuanlin, was a native of Nielu in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 八世祖承，永嘉之亂，討陳敏有功，封柴桑縣侯，除宜都郡守。

translations.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Cheng, during the chaos of Yongjia, had merit in suppressing Chen Min and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chaisang and appointed Administrator of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: His eighth-generation ancestor Cheng, during the Yongjia turmoil, earned merit in suppressing Chen Min, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chaisang, and appointed administrator of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 尋卒官，子孫因居江陵。

translations.literal: Soon he died in office, and his descendants therefore settled in Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in office, and his descendants thereupon settled in Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 父高之，梁山陰令。

translations.literal: His father Gao Zhi was Magistrate of Liangshan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gao Zhi served as magistrate of Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 懍少聰敏，好讀書，晝夜不倦。

translations.literal: Lin from youth was quick and clever, fond of reading, and day and night never weary.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Lin was quick-witted and fond of reading, never weary day or night.

sentences.zh: 語輒引古事，鄉里呼為小兒學士。

translations.literal: When he spoke he always cited ancient affairs, and his village called him the young scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke he cited events from antiquity, and his neighbors called him the boy scholar.

sentences.zh: 梁普通六年，舉秀才，以不及二宮元會，例不對策。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Putong of Liang he was recommended as a xiucai; because he did not reach the New Year assembly at the two palaces, by precedent he did not undergo the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Putong of Liang he was recommended as a xiucai; because he failed to attend the New Year assembly at the two palaces, by precedent he was not examined at court.

sentences.zh: 及梁元帝鎮荊州，謂長史劉之遴曰：「貴鄉多士，為舉一有意少年。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang governed Jing Province, he said to Chief Clerk Liu Zhilin, "Your noble district has many scholars—recommend one promising youth for me.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang governed Jing Province, he told Chief Clerk Liu Zhilin, "Your district has many scholars—recommend one promising youth for me.

sentences.zh: 」之遴以懍應命。

translations.literal: Zhilin nominated Lin in response to the order.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilin nominated Lin in response.

sentences.zh: 卽日引見，令兼記室。

translations.literal: That same day he was summoned for audience and appointed acting Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was presented at audience and appointed acting secretary.

sentences.zh: 嘗夕被召宿省，使制《龍川廟碑》，一夜便就，詰朝呈上。

translations.literal: Once in the evening he was summoned to lodge at the secretariat and ordered to compose the 《Stele for Longchuan Temple》; within one night it was finished, and at dawn he presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was summoned in the evening to lodge at the secretariat and ordered to compose the 《Stele for Longchuan Temple》; he finished it in a single night and presented it at dawn.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝歎美之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang sighed in admiration of it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang praised it with admiration.

sentences.zh: 及移鎮江州，以懍為刑獄參軍，兼掌書記。

translations.literal: When he transferred his garrison to Jiang Province, he made Lin Criminal Affairs Aide and additionally put him in charge of secretarial records.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince transferred his garrison to Jiang Province, he appointed Lin Criminal Affairs Aide and also put him in charge of secretarial records.

sentences.zh: 歷臨汝、建成、廣晉三縣令。

translations.literal: He successively served as Magistrate of the three counties of Linru, Jiancheng, and Guangjin.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as magistrate of Linru, Jiancheng, and Guangjin.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂去職。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he left office to mourn.

sentences.zh: 哭輒嘔血，兩旬之內，絕而復蘇者三。

translations.literal: When he wept he always vomited blood; within twenty days he lost consciousness and revived three times.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he wept he vomited blood; within twenty days he lost consciousness and revived three times.

sentences.zh: 每有羣烏數千，集於廬舍，候哭而來，哭止而去。

translations.literal: Each time several thousand crows would gather at the mourning hut, arriving when he began to weep and departing when the weeping ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Each time several thousand crows would gather at his mourning hut, arriving when he wept and departing when his weeping ceased.

sentences.zh: 時論稱之，以為孝感所致。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion praised this, considering it brought about by filial feeling moving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion held that this was brought about by his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝重牧荊州，以懍為別駕、江陵令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang again governed Jing Province, he made Lin Vice Administrator and Magistrate of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang again took up the governorship of Jing Province, he appointed Lin Vice Administrator and magistrate of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 及帝卽位，擢為尚書侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Emperor took the throne, he was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Lin was promoted to attendant gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又手詔曰：「昔扶柳開國，止曰故人，西鄉胙土，本由賓客。

translations.literal: He also issued a personal edict, saying, "Formerly Fuli opened a state with the title 'old acquaintance'; Xixiang received fief-land originally as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: He also issued a personal edict, saying, "In former times Fuli received a state and was called merely an old acquaintance; Xixiang received his fief originally as a guest.

sentences.zh: 況事涉勳庸，而無爵賞？

translations.literal: How much more when the matter touches merit and achievement, yet there are no title and reward?
translations.idiomatic: How much more when merit and service are involved, yet no title or reward has been granted?

sentences.zh: 尚書侍郎宗懍，亟有帷幄之謀，誠深股肱之寄。

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat Zong Lin has repeatedly had plans within the command tent and truly holds a deep charge as my right arm and thigh.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat Zong Lin has repeatedly advised me in council and truly holds my deepest trust.

sentences.zh: 從我於邁，多歷歲時。

translations.literal: He has followed me on my journey through many years.
translations.idiomatic: He has followed me on many a journey over many years.

sentences.zh: 可封信安縣侯，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: He may be enfeoffed as Marquis of Xin'an with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He is to be enfeoffed as Marquis of Xin'an with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 」累遷吏部郎中、五兵尚書、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel, Minister of the Five Arms, and Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel, Minister of the Five Arms, and Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 初侯景平後，梁元帝議還建業，唯懍勸都渚宮，以其鄉里在荊州故也。

translations.literal: At first, after Hou Jing was suppressed, Emperor Yuan of Liang debated returning to Jianye; Lin alone urged establishing the capital at Zhugong Palace, because his home region was in Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing's rebellion was suppressed, Emperor Yuan of Liang debated returning the capital to Jianye; Lin alone urged him to remain at Zhugong Palace, because his own homeland was in Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 及江陵平，與王褒等入關。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified, he entered the Pass with Wang Bao and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, he entered the Pass with Wang Bao and others.

sentences.zh: 太祖以懍名重南土，甚禮之。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor, because Lin's name carried great weight in the South, treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Because Lin's reputation stood high in the south, the Grand Preceptor treated him with great courtesy.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Director with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, Lin was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Director with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 世宗卽位，又與王褒等在麟趾殿刊定羣書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, he again joined Wang Bao and others in the Linzhi Hall to collate the corpus of books.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Lin again joined Wang Bao and others at the Linzhi Hall to collate the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 數蒙宴賜。

translations.literal: He repeatedly received feasts and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly honored at banquets and granted gifts.

sentences.zh: 保定中卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: He died during Baoding at the age of sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Baoding era at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collected writings in twenty scrolls, circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works of twenty scrolls in circulation.

sentences.zh: 劉璠字寶義，沛國沛人也。

translations.literal: Liu Fan, courtesy name Baoyi, was a man of Pei in the Pei State.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fan, whose courtesy name was Baoyi, was a native of Pei in Pei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 六世祖敏，以永嘉喪亂，徙居廣陵。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Min, on account of the calamities of Yongjia, moved and settled in Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Min, during the Yongjia disasters, moved the family to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 父臧，性方正，篤志好學，居家以孝聞。

translations.literal: His father Zang was upright in nature, steadfast in purpose and fond of learning, and at home was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zang was upright by nature, steadfast and devoted to learning, and was known at home for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，為著作郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian of Liang he served as Gentleman of the Masters of Composition.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianjian reign of Liang he served as gentleman of the Masters of Composition.

sentences.zh: 璠九歲而孤，居喪合禮。

translations.literal: Fan at nine years lost his father; in mourning he was fully observant of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Fan lost his father at nine; in mourning he conducted himself in full accord with ritual.

sentences.zh: 少好讀書，兼善文筆。

translations.literal: From youth he loved reading and was also skilled with brush and writing.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved reading and was also skilled with the pen.

sentences.zh: 年十七，為上黃侯蕭曄所器重。

translations.literal: At seventeen he was greatly valued by Marquis of Shanghuang Xiao Ye.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he won the esteem of Marquis of Shanghuang Xiao Ye.

sentences.zh: 范陽張綰，梁之外戚，才高口辯，見推於世。
