translations.literal: Zhang Wan of Fanyang, a kinsman by marriage of Liang, was talented and quick-tongued, and was honored by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wan of Fanyang, a kinsman of the Liang house by marriage, was brilliant and eloquent and widely admired.

sentences.zh: 以曄之懿貴，亦假借之。

translations.literal: Because of Ye's lofty nobility, he also presumed upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Ye's eminent rank, Zhang also presumed upon him.

sentences.zh: 璠年少未仕，而負才使氣，不為之屈。

translations.literal: Fan was young and had not yet entered office, yet proud of his talent and willful in spirit, he would not submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was young and held no office, yet proud of his talent and high-spirited, he would not submit to Zhang.

sentences.zh: 綰嘗于新渝侯坐，因酒後詬京兆杜騫曰：「寒士不遜。

translations.literal: Wan once at a gathering of Marquis of Xinyu, while drunk, reviled Du Juan of Jingzhao, saying, "The cold-clad scholar knows no deference.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a gathering of Marquis of Xinyu, Zhang, while drunk, insulted Du Juan of Jingzhao, saying, "This poor scholar knows no deference.

sentences.zh: 」璠厲色曰：「此坐誰非寒士？

translations.literal: Fan with stern countenance said, "Who at this table is not a cold-clad scholar?
translations.idiomatic: Fan said sharply, "Who at this gathering is not a poor scholar?

sentences.zh: 」璠本意在綰，而曄以為屬己，辭色不平。

translations.literal: Fan's intent had truly been Zhang, but Ye thought it referred to himself and his expression and tone were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's remark was aimed at Zhang, but Ye thought it referred to himself and his manner turned hostile.

sentences.zh: 璠曰：「何王之門不可曳長裾也！

translations.literal: Fan said, "At which prince's gate may one not drag a long skirt?
translations.idiomatic: Fan said, "At which prince's gate may one not freely sweep one's robes?

sentences.zh: 」遂拂衣而去。

translations.literal: He thereupon shook out his robes and departed.
translations.idiomatic: With that he shook out his robes and left.

sentences.zh: 曄辭謝之，乃止。

translations.literal: Ye apologized to him, and only then did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: Ye apologized, and Fan was mollified.

sentences.zh: 後隨曄在淮南，璠母在建康遘疾，璠弗之知。

translations.literal: Later, following Ye in Huainan, Fan's mother in Jiankang fell ill; Fan did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while accompanying Ye in Huainan, Fan's mother fell ill in Jiankang, and Fan knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 嘗忽一日舉身楚痛，尋而家信至，雲其母病。

translations.literal: Once, suddenly one day his whole body ached with pain; soon thereafter word from home arrived, saying his mother was ill.
translations.idiomatic: One day his whole body suddenly ached with pain; soon a letter from home arrived saying his mother was ill.

sentences.zh: 璠卽號泣戒道，絕而又蘇。

translations.literal: Fan immediately wailed and prepared to depart on the road; he lost consciousness and revived.
translations.idiomatic: Fan immediately broke into wailing and prepared to hurry home; he lost consciousness, then revived.

sentences.zh: 當身痛之辰，卽母死之日也。

translations.literal: The day of his bodily pain was precisely the day of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: The day of his bodily pain was the very day of his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 居喪毀瘠，遂感風氣。

translations.literal: In mourning he wasted away, and thereupon contracted a rheumatic disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he wasted away until he contracted a rheumatic ailment.

sentences.zh: 服闋後一年，猶杖而後起，及曄終於毗陵，故吏多分散，璠獨奉曄喪還都，墳成乃退。

translations.literal: A year after the mourning period ended, he still needed a staff to rise; when Ye died at Piling, former subordinates mostly dispersed, but Fan alone escorted Ye's coffin back to the capital and only withdrew after the tomb was completed.
translations.idiomatic: A year after mourning ended he still needed a staff to rise. When Ye died at Piling, most of his former subordinates dispersed, but Fan alone escorted Ye's coffin to the capital and only withdrew after the tomb was finished.

sentences.zh: 梁簡文時在東宮，遇曄素重，諸不送者皆被劾責，唯璠獨被優賞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jian of Liang was in the Eastern Palace, because Ye had been greatly esteemed, all who did not escort the funeral were investigated and punished; Fan alone received special reward.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Jian of Liang was in the Eastern Palace, because Ye had been greatly favored, all who failed to escort his funeral were censured and punished; Fan alone received special commendation.

sentences.zh: 解褐王國常侍，非其好也。

translations.literal: Upon first taking office he became Attendant of the Prince's Kingdom—this was not his preference.
translations.idiomatic: His first appointment was as attendant in a princely domain—not to his taste.

sentences.zh: 璠少慷慨，好功名，志欲立事邊城，不樂隨牒平進。

translations.literal: Fan from youth was ardent and generous, fond of fame and achievement; his ambition was to accomplish deeds on the border, and he did not delight in advancing through routine appointments.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Fan was ardent and ambitious, seeking fame and achievement; he meant to make his name on the frontier and had no taste for step-by-step promotion through routine posts.

sentences.zh: 會宜豐侯蕭循出為北徐州刺史，卽請為其輕車府主簿，兼記室參軍，又領刑獄。

translations.literal: It happened that Marquis of Yifeng Xiao Xun went out as Governor of Northern Xu Province; Fan immediately requested to serve as Chief Clerk in his Light Chariots Office, concurrently as Recording Secretary, and additionally in charge of criminal matters.
translations.idiomatic: When Marquis of Yifeng Xiao Xun was appointed governor of Northern Xu Province, Fan immediately requested to serve as chief clerk in his light-chariots office, concurrently as recording secretary, and additionally in charge of criminal matters.

sentences.zh: 循為梁州，除信武府記室參軍，領南鄭令。

translations.literal: When Xun governed Liang Province, Fan was appointed Recording Secretary in the Trustworthy Martial Office and additionally served as Magistrate of Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun was assigned to Liang Province, Fan was appointed recording secretary in the Trustworthy Martial Office and additionally served as magistrate of Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 又板為中記室，補華陽太守。

translations.literal: He was further appointed by written commission as Middle Recording Secretary and supplemental Administrator of Huayang.
translations.idiomatic: He was further commissioned as middle recording secretary and appointed supplemental administrator of Huayang.

sentences.zh: 屬侯景度江，梁室大亂，循以璠有才略，甚親委之。

translations.literal: At the time when Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze, the house of Liang fell into great disorder; Xun, because Fan had talent and strategy, greatly trusted and relied upon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze and the Liang house fell into chaos, Xun, recognizing Fan's talent and strategic ability, placed great trust in him.

sentences.zh: 時寇難繁興，未有所定。

translations.literal: At the time rebellions and disasters arose one after another, and nothing was yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellions and disasters arose one after another, and nothing was yet decided.

sentences.zh: 璠乃喟然賦詩以見志。

translations.literal: Fan thereupon sighed and composed poetry to express his resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Fan thereupon sighed and composed a poem to declare his intent.

sentences.zh: 其末章曰：「隨會平王室，夷吾匡霸功。

translations.literal: Its final stanza reads: "Sui Hui pacified the royal house; Yi Wu upheld the hegemonic achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The final stanza reads: "Sui Hui pacified the royal house; Yi Wu upheld the hegemonic achievement.

sentences.zh: 虛薄無時用，徒然慕昔風。

translations.literal: Insignificant and of no use in the times, vainly I admire the manners of old.
translations.idiomatic: Insignificant and useless in these times, I vainly admire the ways of old.

sentences.zh: 」循開府，置佐史，以璠為諮議參軍，仍領記室。

translations.literal: Xun opened a grand office, appointed assistant scribes, made Fan Advisory General, and additionally put him in charge of the recording office.
translations.idiomatic: Xun opened a grand office, appointed assistant scribes, made Fan advisory general, and additionally put him in charge of the recording office.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝承制，授樹功將軍、鎮西府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed imperial authority and appointed him General Who Establishes Merit and Advisory General in the Pacify-the-West Office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed imperial authority and appointed him General Who Establishes Merit and advisory general in the Pacify-the-West Office.

sentences.zh: 賜書曰：「鄧禹文學，尚或執戈；

translations.literal: He granted a letter saying: "Deng Yu was a man of letters, yet still took up arms;
translations.idiomatic: He sent a letter saying: "Deng Yu was a scholar, yet still took up arms;

sentences.zh: 葛洪書生，且雲破賊。

translations.literal: Ge Hong was a scholar, and was said to have broken the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong was a bookish man, yet was said to have routed the bandits.

sentences.zh: 前修無遠，屬望良深。

translations.literal: The eminent of former ages are not far removed; my expectations of you run very deep.
translations.idiomatic: The great men of former ages are not far away; my hopes for you run very deep.

sentences.zh: 」梁元帝尋又以循紹鄱陽之封，且為雍州刺史，復以璠為循平北府司馬。

translations.literal: Soon Emperor Yuan also had Xun inherit the fief of Poyang and appointed him Governor of Yong Province; Fan was again made Pacify-the-North Marshall on Xun's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Emperor Yuan also had Xun inherit the fief of Poyang and appointed him governor of Yong Province; Fan was again made marshal of Xun's Pacify-the-North Office.

sentences.zh: 及武陵王紀稱制於蜀，以璠為中書侍郎，屢遣召璠，使者八返，乃至蜀。

translations.literal: When Prince of Wuling Ji assumed imperial authority in Shu, he appointed Fan as Vice Director of the Secretariat and repeatedly summoned him; the envoy returned eight times before Fan finally came to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Wuling Ji assumed imperial authority in Shu, he appointed Fan vice director of the Secretariat and repeatedly summoned him; the envoy returned eight times before Fan finally reached Shu.

sentences.zh: 又以為黃門侍郎，令長史劉孝勝深布腹心。

translations.literal: He was further made Vice Director of the Yellow Gates; Ji had Chief Administrator Liu Xiaosheng confide deeply in him.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made vice director of the Yellow Gates, and Ji had chief administrator Liu Xiaosheng confide deeply in him.

sentences.zh: 使工畫《陳平度河歸漢圖》以遺之。

translations.literal: He had craftsmen paint the 《Chen Ping Crosses the River and Returns to Han》 and present it to him.
translations.idiomatic: He had craftsmen paint the 《Chen Ping Crosses the River and Returns to Han》 and present it to him.

sentences.zh: 璠苦求還。

translations.literal: Fan earnestly begged to return.
translations.idiomatic: Fan earnestly begged to be allowed to leave.

sentences.zh: 中記室韋登私曰：「殿下忍而蓄憾，足下不留，將

translations.literal: Middle Recording Secretary Wei Deng said privately: "His Highness restrains himself yet harbors resentment; if you do not stay, it will
translations.idiomatic: Middle recording secretary Wei Deng said privately: "His Highness restrains himself yet harbors resentment; if you do not stay, it will

translations.literal: (come)
translations.idiomatic: (the character 至, here emended to 致)

sentences.zh: 〔致〕大禍。

translations.literal: [bring] great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: bring great calamity.

sentences.zh: 脫使盜遮於葭萌，則卿殆矣。

translations.literal: If bandits should intercept you at Jiameng, you would be in mortal danger.
translations.idiomatic: If bandits should waylay you at Jiameng, you would be in mortal danger.

sentences.zh: 孰若共構大廈，使身名俱美哉。

translations.literal: How much better to build a great edifice together and make both body and name beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: How much better to build a great edifice together and win honor for both body and name!

sentences.zh: 」璠正色曰：「卿欲緩頰於我耶？

translations.literal: Fan with stern countenance said: "Do you wish to play advocate for me?
translations.idiomatic: Fan said sternly: "Do you wish to plead on my behalf?

sentences.zh: 我與府侯，分義已定。

translations.literal: My bond with the Marquis has been fixed by shared duty.
translations.idiomatic: My bond with the Marquis is fixed by shared duty.

sentences.zh: 豈以寵辱夷險，易其心乎？

translations.literal: How could favor or disgrace, ease or peril, change my heart?
translations.idiomatic: How could favor or disgrace, ease or peril, change my heart?

sentences.zh: 丈夫立志，當死生以之耳。

translations.literal: A man who sets his will should hold to it through life and death.
translations.idiomatic: A man who sets his will should hold to it through life and death.

sentences.zh: 殿下方布大義於天下，終不逞志於一人。

translations.literal: Your Highness is now spreading great righteousness across the realm; in the end you will not indulge personal spite against one man.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is now spreading great righteousness across the realm; in the end you will not indulge personal spite against one man.

sentences.zh: 」紀知必不為己用，乃厚其贈而遣之。

translations.literal: Ji knew Fan would never serve his purposes, so he enriched his parting gifts and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Ji knew Fan would never serve his purposes, so he enriched his parting gifts and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 臨別，紀又解其佩刀贈璠曰：「想見物思人。

translations.literal: At parting Ji again unfastened his girdle knife and gave it to Fan, saying: "When you see this object, think of me.
translations.idiomatic: At parting Ji again unfastened his girdle knife and gave it to Fan, saying: "When you see this object, think of me.

sentences.zh: 」璠對曰：「敢不奉揚威靈，尅剪姦宄。

translations.literal: Fan replied: "How dare I not uphold your august authority and cut down treacherous evildoers?
translations.idiomatic: Fan replied: "How dare I not uphold your august authority and cut down treacherous evildoers?

sentences.zh: 」紀於是遣使就拜循為益州刺史，封隨郡王，以璠為循府長史，加蜀郡太守。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ji sent envoys to appoint Xun on the spot as Governor of Yi Province, enfeoff him as Prince of Suixiang, and make Fan Chief Administrator on Xun's staff, with the additional post of Administrator of Shu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Ji sent envoys to appoint Xun on the spot as governor of Yi Province, enfeoff him as Prince of Suixiang, and make Fan chief administrator on Xun's staff, with the additional post of administrator of Shu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 還至白馬西，屬達奚武軍已至南鄭，璠不得入城，遂降於武。

translations.literal: When he returned west of Baima, Daxi Wu's army had already reached Nanzheng; Fan could not enter the city and thereupon surrendered to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned west of Baima, Daxi Wu's army had already reached Nanzheng; Fan could not enter the city and thereupon surrendered to Wu.

sentences.zh: 太祖素聞其名，先誡武曰：「勿使劉璠死也。

translations.literal: The Great Ancestor had long known Fan's reputation and beforehand admonished Wu: "Do not let Liu Fan die.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Ancestor had long known Fan's reputation and beforehand admonished Wu: "Do not let Liu Fan die.

sentences.zh: 」故武先令璠赴闕。

translations.literal: Therefore Wu first had Fan proceed to the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Wu first had Fan proceed to the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 璠至，太祖見之如舊。

translations.literal: When Fan arrived, the Great Ancestor received him as of old.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan arrived, the Great Ancestor received him as of old.

sentences.zh: 謂僕射申徽曰：「劉璠佳士，古人何以過之。

translations.literal: He said to the Vice Director Shen Hui: "Liu Fan is a fine gentleman; how could the ancients surpass him?
translations.idiomatic: He said to vice director Shen Hui: "Liu Fan is a fine gentleman; how could the ancients surpass him?

sentences.zh: 」徽曰：「昔晉主滅吳，利在二陸。

translations.literal: Hui said: "Formerly when the Jin ruler destroyed Wu, the gain lay in the two Lus.
translations.idiomatic: Hui said: "Formerly when the Jin ruler destroyed Wu, the gain lay in the two Lus.

sentences.zh: 明公今平梁漢，得一劉璠也。

translations.literal: Your Excellency today in pacifying Liang and Han has gained one Liu Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Your Excellency today in pacifying Liang and Han has gained one Liu Fan.

sentences.zh: 」時南鄭尚拒守未下，達奚武請屠之，太祖將許焉，唯令全璠一家而已。

translations.literal: At the time Nanzheng still held out and had not fallen; Daxi Wu requested that it be put to the sword, and the Great Ancestor was about to consent, ordering only that Fan's household be spared.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Nanzheng still held out and had not fallen; Daxi Wu requested that it be put to the sword, and the Great Ancestor was about to consent, ordering only that Fan's household be spared.

sentences.zh: 璠乃請之于朝，太祖怒而不許。

translations.literal: Fan then pleaded with the court, and the Great Ancestor was angered and refused.
translations.idiomatic: Fan then pleaded at court, and the Great Ancestor was angered and refused.

sentences.zh: 璠泣而固請，移時不退。

translations.literal: Fan wept and firmly persisted in his plea, standing for a long time without withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: Fan wept and firmly persisted in his plea, standing before the throne for a long time without withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 柳仲禮侍側曰：「此烈士也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhongli, standing in attendance, said: "This is a man of heroic resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhongli, standing in attendance, said: "This is a man of heroic resolve.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「事人當如此。

translations.literal: The Great Ancestor said: "This is how one should serve one's lord.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Ancestor said: "This is how one should serve one's lord.

sentences.zh: 」遂許之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he granted the request.

sentences.zh: 城竟獲全，璠之力也。

translations.literal: The city was in the end completely spared; this was Fan's doing.
translations.idiomatic: The city was in the end completely spared; this was Fan's doing.

sentences.zh: 太祖旣納蕭循之降，又許其反國。

translations.literal: The Great Ancestor, having accepted Xiao Xun's surrender, also promised to let him return to his state.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Ancestor, having accepted Xiao Xun's surrender, also promised to let him return to his state.

sentences.zh: 循至長安累月，未之遣也。

translations.literal: Xun had been in Chang'an for months, yet was still not sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had been in Chang'an for months, yet was still not sent back.

sentences.zh: 璠因侍宴，太祖曰：「我于古誰比？

translations.literal: At a banquet where Fan was in attendance, the Great Ancestor said: "To whom among the ancients might I be compared?
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet where Fan was in attendance, the Great Ancestor said: "To whom among the ancients might I be compared?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「常以公命世英主，湯、武莫逮；

translations.literal: He replied: "I always regarded Your Excellency as a heaven-sent heroic ruler whom Tang and Wu could not match;
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "I always regarded Your Excellency as a heaven-sent heroic ruler whom Tang and Wu could not match;

sentences.zh: 今日所見，曾齊桓、晉文之不若。

translations.literal: but what I see today falls even short of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: but what I see today falls even short of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「我不得比湯、武，望與伊、周為匹，何桓、文之不若乎？

translations.literal: The Great Ancestor said: "I cannot compare myself to Tang and Wu; I hope to stand with Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou; how can I fall short of Duke Huan and Duke Wen?
translations.idiomatic: The Great Ancestor said: "I cannot compare myself to Tang and Wu; I hope to stand with Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou; how can I fall short of Duke Huan and Duke Wen?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「齊桓存三亡國，晉文不失信于伐原。

translations.literal: He replied: "Duke Huan of Qi restored three perished states; Duke Wen of Jin did not break faith over the campaign against Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Duke Huan of Qi restored three perished states; Duke Wen of Jin did not break faith over the campaign against Yuan.

sentences.zh: 」語未終，太祖撫掌曰：「我解爾意，欲激我耳。

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking, the Great Ancestor clapped his hands and said: "I understand your meaning; you mean to stir me on.
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished speaking, the Great Ancestor clapped his hands and said: "I understand your meaning; you mean to stir me on.

sentences.zh: 」於是卽命遣循。

translations.literal: Thereupon he immediately ordered that Xun be sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he immediately ordered that Xun be sent back.

sentences.zh: 循請與璠俱還，太祖不許。

translations.literal: Xun requested that Fan return with him, but the Great Ancestor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Xun requested that Fan return with him, but the Great Ancestor did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 以璠為中外府記室，尋遷黃門侍郎、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Fan was appointed recording secretary in the Central and Outer Office; soon he was promoted to Vice Director of the Yellow Gates with the status of Three Grand Equivalents.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was appointed recording secretary in the Central and Outer Office; soon he was promoted to vice director of the Yellow Gates with the status of Three Grand Equivalents.

sentences.zh: 嘗臥疾居家，對雪興感，乃作《雪賦》以遂志云。

translations.literal: Once, while ill at home, stirred by the sight of snow, he composed the 《Rhapsody on Snow》 to give voice to his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while ill at home, stirred by the sight of snow, he composed the 《Rhapsody on Snow》 to give voice to his intent.

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：

translations.literal: Its words read:
translations.idiomatic: Its words read:

sentences.zh: 天地否閉，凝而成雪。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth closed in mutual obstruction; breath congealed and became snow.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth closed in mutual obstruction; breath congealed and became snow.

sentences.zh: 應乎玄冬之辰，在於冱寒之節。

translations.literal: It answers to the season of deep winter, falling in the months of extreme cold.
translations.idiomatic: It answers to the season of deep winter, falling in the months of extreme cold.

sentences.zh: 蒼雲暮同，嚴風曉別。

translations.literal: Dark clouds at dusk blend together; harsh winds at dawn part and go.
translations.idiomatic: Dark clouds at dusk blend together; harsh winds at dawn part and go.

sentences.zh: 散亂徘徊，雰霏皎潔。

translations.literal: Scattered and drifting, swirling about; fine flakes gleam pure and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Scattered and drifting, swirling about; fine flakes gleam pure and bright.

sentences.zh: 違朝陽之暄煦，就陵陰之慘烈。

translations.literal: Turning from the morning sun's warm radiance, it settles upon the shaded slopes' bitter chill.
translations.idiomatic: Turning from the morning sun's warm radiance, it settles upon the shaded slopes' bitter chill.

sentences.zh: 若乃雪山峙於流沙之右，雪宮建於碣石之東。

translations.literal: Consider how a snow mountain rises west of the drifting sands, and a snow palace stands east of Jieshi.
translations.idiomatic: Consider how a snow mountain rises west of the drifting sands, and a snow palace stands east of Jieshi.

sentences.zh: 混二儀而竝色，覆萬有而皆空。

translations.literal: Blending the two primal powers into one hue, it covers the ten thousand beings and empties all.
translations.idiomatic: Blending heaven and earth into one hue, it covers the ten thousand beings and empties all.

sentences.zh: 埋沒河山之上，籠罩寰宇之中。

translations.literal: Entombing river and hill, shrouding all within the cosmos.
translations.idiomatic: Entombing river and hill, shrouding all within the cosmos.

sentences.zh: 日馭潛於蒙泛，地險失於華、嵩。

translations.literal: The sun's chariot hides beneath the vast whiteness; mountain landmarks vanish along with Hua and Song.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's chariot hides beneath the vast whiteness; mountain landmarks vanish along with Hua and Song.

sentences.zh: 旣奪朱而成素，實矯異而為同。

translations.literal: Having wrested red into plain white, it truly transforms difference into sameness.
translations.idiomatic: Having wrested red into plain white, it truly transforms difference into sameness.

sentences.zh: 始飄颻而稍落，遂紛糅而無窮。

translations.literal: At first drifting lightly, then settling bit by bit, until it heaped in endless profusion.
translations.idiomatic: At first drifting lightly, then settling bit by bit, until it heaped in endless profusion.

sentences.zh: 縈回兮瑣散，暠皓兮溟蒙。

translations.literal: Whirling round in fine scatter; blazing white through mist and gloom.
translations.idiomatic: Whirling round in fine scatter; blazing white through mist and gloom.

sentences.zh: 綏綏兮颯颯，瀌瀌兮渢渢。

translations.literal: Softly, softly; rustling, rustling; drifting, drifting; swirling, swirling.
translations.idiomatic: Softly, softly; rustling, rustling; drifting, drifting; swirling, swirling.

sentences.zh: 因高兮累仞，藉少兮成豐。

translations.literal: Building by degrees from the heights; amassing from little into abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Building by degrees from the heights; amassing from little into abundance.

sentences.zh: 曉分光而映淨，夜合影而通朧。

translations.literal: By dawn it divides the light and reflects purity; by night it gathers shadows into hazy unity.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn it divides the light and reflects purity; by night it gathers shadows into hazy unity.

sentences.zh: 似北荒之明月，若西昆之閬風。

translations.literal: Like the bright moon of the far northern wilds; like the Lang-feng breeze of Mount Kun in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Like the bright moon of the far northern wilds; like the Lang-feng breeze of Mount Kun in the west.

sentences.zh: 爾乃憑集異區，遭隨所適。

translations.literal: Then it drifts wherever different regions gather it, meeting each place as fate directs.
translations.idiomatic: Then it drifts wherever different regions gather it, meeting each place as fate directs.

sentences.zh: 遇物淪形，觸途湮跡。

translations.literal: Where it meets things, forms are drowned; whatever path it touches, traces are erased.
translations.idiomatic: Where it meets things, forms are drowned; whatever path it touches, traces are erased.

sentences.zh: 何淨穢之可分，豈高卑之能擇。

translations.literal: How can clean and foul be distinguished? How could it choose high or low?
translations.idiomatic: How can clean and foul be distinguished? How could it choose high or low?

sentences.zh: 體不常消，質無定白。

translations.literal: Its form does not vanish at once; its substance has no fixed whiteness.
translations.idiomatic: Its form does not vanish at once; its substance has no fixed whiteness.

sentences.zh: 深谷夏凝，小山春積。

translations.literal: Deep valleys freeze even in summer; low hills hold snow still in spring.
translations.idiomatic: Deep valleys freeze even in summer; low hills hold snow still in spring.

sentences.zh: 偶仙宮而為絳，值河濱而成赤。

translations.literal: By chance at an immortal palace it turns crimson; on reaching a riverbank it becomes red.
translations.idiomatic: By chance at an immortal palace it turns crimson; on reaching a riverbank it becomes red.

sentences.zh: 廣則彌綸而交四海，小則淅瀝而緣間隙。

translations.literal: Broadly it spreads to knit the four seas; narrowly it trickles through every gap.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly it spreads to knit the four seas; narrowly it trickles through every gap.

sentences.zh: 淺則不過二寸，大則平地一尺。

translations.literal: Shallow falls never exceed two inches; deep drifts on level ground reach a foot.
translations.idiomatic: Shallow falls never exceed two inches; deep drifts on level ground reach a foot.

sentences.zh: 乃為五穀之精，寔長衆川之魄。

translations.literal: It is the essence of the five grains, truly the sustaining soul of the myriad rivers.
translations.idiomatic: It is the essence of the five grains, truly the sustaining soul of the myriad rivers.

sentences.zh: 大壑所以朝宗，洪波資其消釋。

translations.literal: Great gorges hold it as tribute to the sovereign river; raging floods rely on it for their dissolving.
translations.idiomatic: Great gorges hold it as tribute to the sovereign river; raging floods rely on it for their dissolving.

sentences.zh: 家有趙王之璧，人聚漢帝之金。

translations.literal: In each house there is a jade disc of the King of Zhao; each person hoards gold of the Han Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In each house there is a jade disc of the King of Zhao; each person hoards gold of the Han Emperor.

sentences.zh: 旣藏牛而沒馬，又冰木而凋林。

translations.literal: Cows are buried and horses submerged; trees are iced over and groves wither.
translations.idiomatic: Cows are buried and horses submerged; trees are iced over and groves wither.

sentences.zh: 已墮白登之指，實愴黃竹之心。

translations.literal: Already fallen under the finger of Baideng; truly pained at heart like the Yellow Bamboo song.
translations.idiomatic: Already fallen under the finger of Baideng; truly pained at heart like the Yellow Bamboo song.

sentences.zh: 楚客埋魂於樹裏，漢使遷饑于海陰。

translations.literal: The Chu guest was buried in soul beneath the trees; the Han envoy endured hunger by the northern sea.
translations.idiomatic: The Chu guest was buried in soul beneath the trees; the Han envoy endured hunger by the northern sea.

sentences.zh: 斃雲中之狡獸，落海上之驚禽。

translations.literal: Cunning beasts of the clouds perish; startled birds of the sea fall.
translations.idiomatic: Cunning beasts of the clouds perish; startled birds of the sea fall.

sentences.zh: 庚辰有七尺之厚，甲子有一丈之深。

translations.literal: In a gengchen year snow piled seven feet deep; in a jiazi year it reached a full ten feet.
translations.idiomatic: In a gengchen year snow piled seven feet deep; in a jiazi year it reached a full ten feet.

sentences.zh: 無復垂霙與雲合，唯有變白作泥沉。

translations.literal: No longer does fine snow mingle with clouds; only whiteness turns to mud and sinks away.
translations.idiomatic: No longer does fine snow mingle with clouds; only whiteness turns to mud and sinks away.

sentences.zh: 本為白雪唱，翻作《白頭吟》。

translations.literal: Originally meant as a song to white snow, it turned instead into the 《White-Haired Lament》.
translations.idiomatic: Originally meant as a song to white snow, it turned instead into the 《White-Haired Lament》.

sentences.zh: 吟曰：昔從天山來，忽與狂風閱。

translations.literal: It recites: Long ago I came from Mount Tian, suddenly to be tested by raging winds.
translations.idiomatic: It recites: Long ago I came from Mount Tian, suddenly to be tested by raging winds.

sentences.zh: 逆河陰而散漫，望衡陽而委絕。

translations.literal: Against the river's northern bank I scattered; gazing toward Hengyang I faded and ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Against the river's northern bank I scattered; gazing toward Hengyang I faded and ceased.

sentences.zh: 朝朝自消盡，夜夜空凝結。

translations.literal: Day by day I melt away; night by night the sky freezes anew.
translations.idiomatic: Day by day I melt away; night by night the sky freezes anew.

sentences.zh: 徒云雪之可賦，竟何賦之能雪。

translations.literal: In vain one says snow can be rhapsodized; what rhapsody could actually whiten snow back?
translations.idiomatic: In vain one says snow can be rhapsodized; what rhapsody could actually whiten snow back?

sentences.zh: 初，蕭循在漢中與蕭紀箋及答國家書、移襄陽文，皆璠之辭也。

translations.literal: Earlier, the letters between Xiao Xun and Xiao Ji in Hanzhong, the replies to the imperial court, and the dispatch to Xiangyang were all Fan's compositions.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the letters exchanged between Xiao Xun and Xiao Ji in Hanzhong, the replies to the imperial court, and the dispatch to Xiangyang were all Fan's compositions.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，授內史中大夫，掌綸誥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat and put in charge of imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, he was appointed grand master of the Palace Secretariat and put in charge of imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 尋封平陽縣子，邑九百戶。

translations.literal: Soon he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Pingyang with a fief of nine hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was enfeoffed as viscount of Pingyang with a fief of nine hundred households.

sentences.zh: 在職清白簡亮，不合于時，左遷同和郡守。

translations.literal: Upright, incorruptible, and plain-spoken in office, he did not fit the temper of the times and was demoted to Administrator of Tonghe Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, incorruptible, and plain-spoken in office, he did not fit the temper of the times and was demoted to administrator of Tonghe Commandery.

sentences.zh: 璠善於撫御，蒞職未期，生羌降附者五百餘家。

translations.literal: Fan was skilled in governing and winning people over; before his term was half done, more than five hundred households of sheng Qiang submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was skilled in governing and winning people over; before his term was half done, more than five hundred households of sheng Qiang submitted.

sentences.zh: 前後郡守多經營以致貲產，唯璠秋毫無所取，妻子竝隨羌俗，食麥衣皮，始終不改。

translations.literal: Former and later commandery administrators mostly schemed to amass wealth; Fan alone took not so much as a hair's breadth, and his wife and children likewise followed Qiang custom, eating barley and wearing hides, never altering this to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Former and later commandery administrators mostly schemed to amass wealth; Fan alone took not so much as a hair's breadth, and his wife and children likewise followed Qiang custom, eating barley and wearing hides, never altering this to the end.

sentences.zh: 洮陽、洪和二郡羌民，常越境詣璠訟理焉。

translations.literal: Qiang people of Taoyang and Honghe commanderies often crossed borders to bring disputes before Fan for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang people of Taoyang and Honghe commanderies often crossed borders to bring disputes before Fan for judgment.

sentences.zh: 其德化為他界所歸仰如此。

translations.literal: Such was the moral transforming influence for which other regions looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the moral transforming influence for which other regions looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 蔡公廣時鎮隴右，嘉璠善政。

translations.literal: When Duke Cai Guang was stationed in Longyou, he praised Fan's excellent governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Cai Guang was stationed in Longyou, he praised Fan's excellent governance.

sentences.zh: 及遷鎮陝州，欲取璠自隨，羌人樂從者七百人。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to guard Shaanzhou, he wished to take Fan with him; seven hundred Qiang who gladly followed went along.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to guard Shaanzhou, he wished to take Fan with him, and seven hundred Qiang gladly followed.

sentences.zh: 聞者莫不歎異。

translations.literal: All who heard of it sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard of it marveled and sighed.

sentences.zh: 陳公純作鎮隴右，引為總管府司錄，甚禮敬之。

translations.literal: When Duke Chen Chun was stationed in Longyou, he summoned Fan as Chief Clerk of the Grand Commandant's Office and treated him with great courtesy and respect.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Chen Chun was stationed in Longyou, he summoned Fan as chief clerk of the grand commandant's office and treated him with great courtesy and respect.

sentences.zh: 天和三年卒，時年五十九。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe he died, at age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Tianhe, at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 著《梁典》三十卷，有集二十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He wrote the 《Records of Liang》 in thirty scrolls; he also had a collected works in twenty scrolls, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the 《Records of Liang》 in thirty scrolls and a collected works in twenty scrolls, both of which circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 子祥嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xiang succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 祥字休徵。

translations.literal: Xiang's courtesy name was Xiuzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's courtesy name was Xiuzheng.

sentences.zh: 幼而聰慧，占對俊辯，賓客見者，皆號神童。

translations.literal: Intelligent from childhood, quick and eloquent in conversation, all guests who met him called him a divine child.
translations.idiomatic: Bright from childhood, quick and eloquent in conversation, every guest who met him hailed him as a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 事嫡母以至孝聞。

translations.literal: In serving his stepmother he was famed for utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He was renowned for the utmost filial piety with which he served his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 其伯父黃門郎璆有名江左，在嶺南，聞而奇之，乃令名祥字休徵。

translations.literal: His uncle Liu Qiu, a Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, was famous south of the Yangzi; residing in Lingnan, when he heard of the boy he marveled at him and had him named Xiang with the courtesy name Xiuzheng.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Liu Qiu, a gentleman of the Yellow Gates famed south of the Yangzi, was in Lingnan; when he heard of the boy he was astonished and had him named Xiang with the courtesy name Xiuzheng.

sentences.zh: 後以字行於世。

translations.literal: Thereafter the courtesy name was used in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he was known in the world by his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 年十歲能屬文，十二通《五經》。

translations.literal: At age ten he could compose prose; at twelve he mastered the 《Five Classics》.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he could compose prose; at twelve he had mastered the 《Five Classics》.

sentences.zh: 解褐梁宜豐侯主簿，遷記室參軍。

translations.literal: Upon entering service he became Chief Clerk to Marquis Yifeng of Liang, and was promoted to Recording Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering service he became chief clerk to Marquis Yifeng of Liang and was later promoted to recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 江陵平，隨例入國。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, he followed the usual practice and entered the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, he followed the usual practice and entered Northern Zhou service.

sentences.zh: 齊公憲以其善於詞令，召為記室。

translations.literal: Duke of Qi Xian, because he was skilled in formal language, summoned him as Recording Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was skilled in formal language, Duke of Qi Xian summoned him as recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 府中書記，皆令掌之。

translations.literal: All the office's written records were put under his charge.
translations.idiomatic: All the office's written records were placed under his charge.

sentences.zh: 尋授都督，封漢安縣子，食邑七百戶，轉從事中郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Commander, enfeoffed as Viscount of Han'an with a fief of seven hundred households, and transferred to Attendant of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed commander, enfeoffed as viscount of Han'an with a fief of seven hundred households, and transferred to attendant of affairs.

sentences.zh: 憲進爵為王，以休徵為王友。

translations.literal: When Xian was promoted to prince, he made Xiuzheng Prince's Friend.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian was promoted to prince, he made Xiuzheng prince's friend.

sentences.zh: 俄除內史上士。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Senior Secretary of the Inner Historian.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed senior secretary of the Inner Historian.

sentences.zh: 高祖東征，休徵陪侍帷幄。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu campaigned east, Xiuzheng attended him within the command tent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu campaigned east, Xiuzheng attended him within the command tent.

sentences.zh: 平齊露布，卽休徵之文也。

translations.literal: The victory bulletin announcing the pacification of Qi was Xiuzheng's composition.
translations.idiomatic: The victory bulletin announcing the pacification of Qi was written by Xiuzheng.

sentences.zh: 累遷車騎大將軍、儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and General with Equal Standing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to general of chariots and cavalry and general with equal standing.

sentences.zh: 尋以去官，領萬年令，未期月，轉長安令。

translations.literal: Soon leaving office, he held the post of Magistrate of Wannian; before a full month had passed, he was transferred to Magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he left office to serve as magistrate of Wannian; before a full month had passed, he was transferred to magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 頻宰二縣，頗獲時譽。

translations.literal: Governing two counties in succession, he won considerable praise at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Governing two counties in succession, he won considerable praise at the time.

sentences.zh: 大象二年，卒于官，時年四十七。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daxiang he died in office, at age forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daxiang he died in office, at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 初，璠所撰《梁典》始就，未及刊定而卒。

translations.literal: Earlier, the 《Records of Liang》 that Fan had compiled was just completed but not yet edited for publication when he died.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Fan had just finished compiling the 《Records of Liang》, but before it could be edited for publication he died.

sentences.zh: 臨終謂休徵曰：「能成我志，其在此書乎。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he told Xiuzheng: "You can fulfill my wish; surely it lies in this book.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he told Xiuzheng: "You can fulfill my wish; surely it lies in this book.

translations.literal: Xiuzheng
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzheng

translations.literal: (begin)
translations.idiomatic: (the character 始, here supplying 始治)

sentences.zh: 〔治〕定繕寫，勒成一家，行於世。

translations.literal: [edit] and finalize copying, compiled it into one authoritative work, and circulated it in the world.
translations.idiomatic: edited, copied, and finalized it into a coherent work that circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 柳霞字子昇，河東解人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xia, courtesy name Zisheng, was a man of Jie in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xia, whose courtesy name was Zisheng, came from Jie in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖卓，晉汝南太守，始自本郡徙居襄陽。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zhuo was Administrator of Runan under Jin and first moved from their native commandery to settle in Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zhuo, administrator of Runan under Jin, was the first to move from their native commandery and settle in Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 祖叔珍，宋員外散騎常侍、義陽內史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shuzhen was Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry under Song and Interior Secretary of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shuzhen served under Song as supernumerary regular attendant of the dispersed cavalry and interior secretary of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 父季遠，梁臨川王諮議參軍、宜都太守。

translations.literal: His father Jiyuan was Advisory General on the staff of Prince of Linchuan of Liang and Administrator of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiyuan was advisory general on the staff of Prince of Linchuan of Liang and administrator of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 霞幼而爽邁，神彩嶷然，髫歲便有成人之量。

translations.literal: Xia from childhood was open and bold, with a lofty bearing; even in his early years he showed the measure of a grown man.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Xia was open and bold, with a lofty bearing; even in his early years he showed the measure of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 篤好文學，動合規矩。

translations.literal: He deeply loved literature; his every action accorded with propriety.
translations.idiomatic: He deeply loved literature, and his every action accorded with propriety.

sentences.zh: 其世父慶遠特器異之。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Qingyuan especially valued and regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His father's elder brother Qingyuan especially valued him and regarded him as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 謂霞曰：「吾昔逮事伯父太尉公，嘗語吾云：『我昨夢汝登一樓，樓甚峻麗，吾以坐席與汝。

translations.literal: He said to Xia: "In the past I had the honor of serving our uncle the Grand Marshal; he once told me: 'Yesterday I dreamed that you climbed a tower, a tower very lofty and splendid, and I gave you my seat.
translations.idiomatic: He said to Xia: "In the past I had the honor of serving our uncle the Grand Marshal; he once told me: 'Yesterday I dreamed that you climbed a tower, very lofty and splendid, and I gave you my seat.

sentences.zh: 汝後名宦必達，恨吾不及見耳。

translations.literal: Your later fame and office will surely be achieved; I regret that I shall not live to see it.
translations.idiomatic: Your later fame and office will surely be achieved; I regret that I shall not live to see it.

sentences.zh: 』吾向聊復晝寢，又夢將昔時座席還以賜汝。

translations.literal: Just now I took a brief nap again, and again dreamed of giving you that former seat as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: Just now I took a brief nap again, and again dreamed of giving you that former seat as a gift.

sentences.zh: 汝之官位，當復及吾。

translations.literal: Your official rank should again reach mine.
translations.idiomatic: Your official rank should again reach mine.

sentences.zh: 特宜勉勵，以應嘉祥也。」

translations.literal: You should especially strive to respond to this auspicious omen."
translations.idiomatic: You should especially strive hard to answer this auspicious omen."

sentences.zh: 梁西昌侯深藻鎮雍州，霞時年十二，以民禮修謁，風儀端肅，進止詳雅。

translations.literal: When Marquis of Xichang Shenzao of Liang was stationed in Yong Province, Xia was twelve; he paid a visit according to common courtesy, with dignified bearing and graceful, measured movements.
translations.idiomatic: When Marquis of Xichang Shenzao of Liang was stationed in Yong Province, Xia was twelve; he paid a visit according to common courtesy, with a dignified bearing and graceful, measured movements.

sentences.zh: 深藻美之，試遣左右踐霞衣裾，欲觀其舉措。

translations.literal: Shenzao admired him and deliberately sent attendants to tread on Xia's robe to observe his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzao admired him and deliberately sent attendants to tread on Xia's robe to observe how he would react.

sentences.zh: 霞徐步稍前，曾不顧眄。

translations.literal: Xia walked slowly a little forward and never once looked back.
translations.idiomatic: Xia walked slowly a little forward and never once looked back.

sentences.zh: 廬陵王續為雍州刺史，辟霞為主簿。

translations.literal: When Prince of Luling Xu was Governor of Yong Province, he recruited Xia as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Luling Xu became governor of Yong Province, he recruited Xia as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 起家平西邵陵王綸府法曹參軍，仍轉外兵，除尚書工部郎。

translations.literal: He began his career as Legal Affairs General on the staff of Prince of Shaoling of the Pacify-the-West Office, then transferred to External Troops, and was appointed Gentleman of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as legal affairs general on the staff of Prince of Shaoling of the Pacify-the-West Office, then transferred to external troops, and was appointed gentleman of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 謝舉時為僕射，引霞與語，甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Xie Ju was then Vice Director; he drew Xia into conversation and greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Ju was then vice director; he drew Xia into conversation and greatly praised him.

sentences.zh: 顧謂人曰：「江漢英靈，見於此矣。」

translations.literal: Turning, he said to others: "The heroic spirit of the Jiang and Han is seen in this man."
translations.idiomatic: Turning to those around him, he said: "The heroic spirit of the Jiang and Han is seen in this man."

sentences.zh: 岳陽王蕭詧蒞雍州，選為治中，尋遷別駕。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yueyang Xiao Cha came to Yong Province, Xia was selected as Chief Administrator and soon promoted to Vice Governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Yueyang Xiao Cha came to Yong Province, Xia was selected as chief administrator and soon promoted to vice governor.

sentences.zh: 及詧於襄陽承制，授霞吏部郎、員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Cha assumed imperial authority at Xiangyang, he appointed Xia Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel and Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha assumed imperial authority at Xiangyang, he appointed Xia gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel and supernumerary regular attendant of the dispersed cavalry.

sentences.zh: 俄遷車騎大將軍、儀同三司、大都督，賜爵聞喜縣公。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry, General with Equal Standing of the Third Rank, Grand Commander, and granted the title Duke of Wenxi County.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to general of chariots and cavalry, general with equal standing of the third rank, and grand commander, and was granted the title duke of Wenxi County.

sentences.zh: 尋進位持節、侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Master with Grand Office and Equal Standing of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was advanced to bearer of the staff, palace attendant, general of agile cavalry, and grand master with grand office and equal standing of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 及蕭詧踐帝位於江陵，以襄陽歸于我。

translations.literal: When Xiao Cha ascended the throne at Jiangling, he returned Xiangyang to us.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha ascended the throne at Jiangling, he returned Xiangyang to us.

sentences.zh: 霞乃辭詧曰：「陛下中興鼎運，龍飛舊楚。

translations.literal: Xia thereupon took leave of Cha, saying: "Your Majesty has revived the imperial destiny and ascended like a dragon in old Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Xia thereupon took leave of Cha, saying: "Your Majesty has revived the imperial destiny and ascended like a dragon in old Chu.

sentences.zh: 臣昔因幸會，早奉名節，理當以身許國，期之始終。

translations.literal: Your subject once, by fortunate chance, early pledged his name and integrity; by right he should devote his body to the state from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject once, by fortunate chance, early pledged his loyalty; by right he should devote himself to the state from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 自晉氏南遷，臣宗族蓋寡。

translations.literal: Since the Jin house moved south, my clan has been few.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin house moved south, my clan has been small.

sentences.zh: 從祖太尉、世父儀同、從父司空，並以位望隆重，遂家于金陵。

translations.literal: A great-uncle who was Grand Marshal, a father's elder brother who was General with Equal Standing, and a father's younger brother who was Minister of Works all, by rank and renown, made their homes in Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: A great-uncle who was grand marshal, a father's elder brother who was general with equal standing, and a father's younger brother who was minister of works all, by rank and renown, made their homes in Jinling.

sentences.zh: 唯留先臣，獨守墳栢。

translations.literal: Only my late father was left behind to guard the ancestral graves alone.
translations.idiomatic: Only my late father was left behind to guard the ancestral graves alone.

sentences.zh: 常誡臣等，使不違此志。

translations.literal: He constantly admonished us not to violate this resolve.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly admonished us never to violate this resolve.

sentences.zh: 今襄陽旣入北朝，臣若陪隨鑾蹕，進則無益塵露，退則有虧先旨。

translations.literal: Now that Xiangyang has entered the Northern Court, if your subject followed the imperial procession, to advance would be of no use like dust and dew, and to withdraw would fall short of my father's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Xiangyang has passed to the Northern Court, if I followed the imperial procession, to go forward would be of no use, like dust and dew, and to stay behind would betray my father's intent.

sentences.zh: 伏願曲垂照鑒，亮臣此心。

translations.literal: I humbly beg you to bend your illumination and discernment and understand this heart of mine.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg you to look upon me with understanding and grant this wish of my heart.

sentences.zh: 」詧重違其志，遂許之。

translations.literal: Cha, loath to go against his resolve, thereupon granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Cha, loath to go against his resolve, thereupon granted his request.

sentences.zh: 因留鄉里，以經籍自娛。

translations.literal: He therefore remained in his native place and amused himself with the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore remained in his native place and amused himself with the classics.

sentences.zh: 太祖、世宗頻有徵命，霞固辭以疾。

translations.literal: The Great Ancestor and Emperor Shizong repeatedly issued summonses, but Xia firmly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Ancestor and Emperor Shizong repeatedly issued summonses, but Xia firmly declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 及詧殂，霞舉哀，行舊君之服。

translations.literal: When Cha died, Xia observed mourning and wore the garb due a former lord.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha died, Xia observed mourning and wore the garb due a former lord.

sentences.zh: 保定中又徵之，霞始入朝。

translations.literal: In Baoding he was summoned again, and Xia finally entered court.
translations.idiomatic: During Baoding he was summoned again, and Xia finally entered court.

sentences.zh: 授使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、霍州諸軍事、霍州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Bearer of the Staff, General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Master with Grand Office and Equal Standing of the Third Rank, Supervisor of All Military Affairs of Huo Province, and Governor of Huo Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed bearer of the staff, general of agile cavalry, grand master with grand office and equal standing of the third rank, supervisor of all military affairs of Huo Province, and governor of Huo Province.

sentences.zh: 霞導民務先以德，再三不用命者，乃微加貶異，示之恥而已。

translations.literal: In guiding the people Xia put virtue first; only for those who repeatedly disobeyed did he lightly impose censure and disgrace to show them shame.
translations.idiomatic: In guiding the people Xia put virtue first; only for those who repeatedly disobeyed did he lightly impose censure and disgrace to shame them.

sentences.zh: 其下感而化之，不復為過。

translations.literal: Those under him were moved and transformed, and no longer committed offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Those under him were moved and transformed, and no longer committed offenses.

sentences.zh: 咸曰；

translations.literal: All said:
translations.idiomatic: All said:

sentences.zh: 「我君仁惠如此，其可欺乎！

translations.literal: "Our lord is so benevolent and gracious - how could he be deceived!
translations.idiomatic: "Our lord is so benevolent and gracious - how could we deceive him!

sentences.zh: 」天和中，卒，時年七十二。

translations.literal: In Tianhe he died, at age seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianhe he died, at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 宣政初，贈金、安二州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanzheng he was posthumously granted the posts of Governor of Jin and Governor of An.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xuanzheng he was posthumously granted the posts of governor of Jin and governor of An.

sentences.zh: 霞有志行。

translations.literal: Xia had resolve and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Xia was a man of resolve and integrity.

sentences.zh: 初為州主簿，其父卒於揚州，霞自襄陽奔赴，六日而至。

translations.literal: When he was first chief clerk of the province, his father died in Yangzhou; Xia rushed from Xiangyang and arrived in six days.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first chief clerk of the province, his father died in Yangzhou; Xia rushed from Xiangyang and arrived in six days.

sentences.zh: 哀感行路，毀瘁殆不可識。

translations.literal: His grief moved passersby on the road; he was so wasted by mourning he was nearly unrecognizable.
translations.idiomatic: His grief moved passersby on the road; he was so wasted by mourning that he was nearly unrecognizable.

sentences.zh: 後奉喪泝江西歸，中流風起，舟中之人，相顧失色。

translations.literal: Later, escorting the coffin up the Yangzi to return west, a wind rose midstream; those in the boat looked at one another in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Later, escorting the coffin up the Yangzi to return west, a wind rose midstream, and those in the boat looked at one another in alarm.

sentences.zh: 霞抱棺號慟，愬天求哀，俄頃之間，風浪止息。

translations.literal: Xia embraced the coffin and wailed in grief, appealing to Heaven for pity; in a moment the wind and waves ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Xia embraced the coffin and wailed in grief, appealing to Heaven for pity; in a moment the wind and waves ceased.

sentences.zh: 其母嘗乳間發疽，醫云：「此病無可救之理，唯得人吮膿，或望微止其痛。

translations.literal: His mother once developed an abscess between her breasts; the physician said: "This illness has no means of cure; only if someone sucks out the pus might one hope slightly to ease the pain.
translations.idiomatic: His mother once developed an abscess between her breasts; the physician said: "This illness has no cure; only if someone sucks out the pus might one hope slightly to ease the pain.

sentences.zh: 」霞應聲卽吮，旬日遂瘳。

translations.literal: Xia at once responded and sucked; in ten days she recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Xia at once responded and did so; within ten days she recovered.

sentences.zh: 咸以為孝感所致。

translations.literal: All regarded it as brought about by filial feeling moving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: All regarded it as brought about by filial devotion moving Heaven.

sentences.zh: 性又溫裕，略無喜慍之容。

translations.literal: His nature was also gentle and generous, with scarcely any look of joy or anger.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was also gentle and generous, with scarcely any look of joy or anger.

sentences.zh: 弘獎名教，未嘗論人之短。

translations.literal: He broadly encouraged the teachings of propriety and never discussed others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: He broadly encouraged the teachings of propriety and never discussed others' faults.

sentences.zh: 尤好施與，家無餘財。

translations.literal: He especially loved giving to others, and his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He especially loved giving to others, and his household had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 臨終遺誡薄葬，其子等竝奉行之。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he left instructions for a simple burial, and his sons all followed them.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he left instructions for a simple burial, and his sons all followed them.

sentences.zh: 有十子，靖、莊最知名。

translations.literal: He had ten sons; Jing and Zhuang were the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He had ten sons; Jing and Zhuang were the most renowned.

sentences.zh: 靖字思休。

translations.literal: Jing's courtesy name was Sihou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's courtesy name was Sihou.

sentences.zh: 少方雅，博覽墳籍。

translations.literal: From youth he was upright and refined, and read widely in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was upright and refined, and read widely in the classics.

sentences.zh: 梁大同末，釋褐武陵王國左常侍，轉法曹行參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Datong of Liang he entered service as Left Regular Attendant of the Kingdom of Wuling, then transferred to Acting Legal Affairs General.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Datong of Liang he entered service as left regular attendant of the Kingdom of Wuling, then transferred to acting legal affairs general.

sentences.zh: 大定初，除尚書度支郎，遷正員郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading he was appointed Gentleman of Revenue in the Secretariat and promoted to Regular Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dading he was appointed gentleman of revenue in the Secretariat and promoted to regular gentleman.

sentences.zh: 隨霞入朝，授大都督，歷河南、德廣二郡守。

translations.literal: Following Xia into court, he was appointed Grand Commander and successively served as Administrator of Henan and Administrator of Deguang.
translations.idiomatic: Following Xia into court, he was appointed grand commander and successively served as administrator of Henan and administrator of Deguang.

sentences.zh: 靖雅達政事，所居皆有治術，吏民畏而愛之。

translations.literal: Jing was refined and adept in governance; wherever he served he had methods of good administration, and officials and people both feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was refined and adept in governance; wherever he served he had methods of good administration, and officials and people both feared and loved him.

sentences.zh: 然性愛閑素，其於名利澹如也。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he loved quiet simplicity; toward fame and profit he was utterly indifferent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by nature he loved quiet simplicity and was utterly indifferent to fame and profit.

sentences.zh: 及秩滿還，便有終焉之志。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned, he already had the resolve to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and he returned home, he already had the resolve to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝踐極，特詔徵之，靖遂以疾固辭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, he issued a special edict summoning him; Jing firmly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, he issued a special edict summoning him, but Jing firmly declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 優遊不仕，閉門自守，所對惟琴書而已。

translations.literal: At leisure and without office, he shut his door and kept to himself; his only companions were the zither and books.
translations.idiomatic: At leisure and without office, he shut his door and kept to himself; his only companions were the zither and books.

sentences.zh: 足不歷園庭，殆將十載。

translations.literal: His feet did not cross the garden court for nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: His feet did not cross the garden court for nearly ten years.

sentences.zh: 子弟等奉之，若嚴君焉。

translations.literal: His sons and younger relatives served him as if he were a stern father.
translations.idiomatic: His sons and younger relatives served him as if he were a stern father.

sentences.zh: 其有過者，靖必下帷自責，於是長幼相率拜謝於庭，靖然後見之，勖以禮法。

translations.literal: When any of them had faults, Jing would always lower the curtain and blame himself; then elders and juniors together would bow in apology in the courtyard, and only then would Jing receive them and exhort them with ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: When any of them had faults, Jing would always lower the curtain and blame himself; then elders and juniors together would bow in apology in the courtyard, and only then would Jing receive them and exhort them with ritual and law.

sentences.zh: 鄉里亦慕而化之。

translations.literal: The neighborhood also admired him and was transformed by his example.
translations.idiomatic: The whole neighborhood admired him and took his example to heart.

sentences.zh: 或有不善者，皆曰：「唯恐柳德廣知也。

translations.literal: If anyone did wrong, they would all say, "I only fear that Liu Deguang might find out."
translations.idiomatic: When anyone did wrong, people would say, "I only fear Liu Deguang might find out."

sentences.zh: 」時論方之王烈。

translations.literal: "Contemporary opinion at the time ranked him with Wang Lie.
translations.idiomatic: "Contemporary opinion ranked him alongside Wang Lie.

sentences.zh: 前後總管到官，皆親至靖家問疾，遂以為故事。

translations.literal: Successive regional commanders, upon taking office, all came in person to Jing's home to inquire after his health, and this became a precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Every regional commander who took office came in person to Jing's home to inquire after his health, and this became an established custom.

sentences.zh: 秦王俊臨州，賚以幾杖，並致衣物。

translations.literal: When Prince Jun of Qin came to the province, he bestowed a folding stool and staff upon him and also sent clothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jun of Qin arrived to govern the province, he presented Jing with a folding stool and staff and also sent him clothing.

sentences.zh: 靖唯受幾杖，餘竝固辭。

translations.literal: Jing accepted only the stool and staff; all the rest he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Jing accepted only the stool and staff and firmly declined everything else.

sentences.zh: 其為當時所重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held in his day.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which his contemporaries held him.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，以壽終。

translations.literal: During the Kaihuang era he died at a full old age.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang reign he died at a ripe old age.

sentences.zh: 莊字思敬。

translations.literal: Zhuang, courtesy name Sijing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang, whose courtesy name was Sijing,

sentences.zh: 器量貞固，有經世之才。

translations.literal: was firm in character and capacity and possessed talent for ordering the age.
translations.idiomatic: was steadfast in character and possessed the talent to govern an age.

sentences.zh: 初仕梁，歷中書舍人、尚書右丞、給事黃門侍郎、尚書吏部郎中、鴻臚太府卿。

translations.literal: He first served the Liang, holding successively the posts of Secretariat Drafter, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, Attendant Within the Gates of the Yellow Gate, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel of the Secretariat, and Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career under the Liang and served successively as Secretariat Drafter, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, Attendant Within the Gates of the Yellow Gate, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and Grand Steward.

sentences.zh: 入隋，位至開府儀同三司、給事黃門侍郎、饒州刺史。

translations.literal: Entering Sui, he rose to Director with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies, Attendant Within the Gates of the Yellow Gate, and Governor of Rao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he rose to Director with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, Attendant Within the Gates of the Yellow Gate, and governor of Rao Province.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：蕭撝、世怡、圓肅、大圜竝有梁之令望也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Xiao Hui, Shiyi, Yuansu, and Dahuan all possessed the eminent reputation of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Xiao Hui, Shiyi, Yuansu, and Dahuan all enjoyed the eminent standing of the Liang court.

sentences.zh: 雖羈旅異國，而終享榮名。

translations.literal: Although they lived as sojourners in a foreign state, in the end they still enjoyed glory and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Though they lived as exiles in a foreign realm, they still won honor and renown in the end.

sentences.zh: 非有茲基，夙懷文質，亦何能至於此乎。

translations.literal: Had they not possessed this foundation and long cherished literary and substantive talent, how could they have reached such heights?
translations.idiomatic: Without that foundation and their lifelong cultivation of learning and substance, how could they have risen so high?

sentences.zh: 方武陵擁衆東下，任撝以蕭何之事，君臣之道旣篤，家國之情亦隆。

translations.literal: When Prince Wuling led his forces eastward, he entrusted Hui with duties like those of Xiao He; the bond between ruler and minister was already deep, and the feeling between family and state was also exalted.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wuling marched east at the head of his army, he entrusted Hui with responsibilities like those of Xiao He; the bond between ruler and minister ran deep, and the ties of family and state stood high.

sentences.zh: 金石不足比其心，河山不足盟其誓。

translations.literal: Metal and stone would not suffice to compare their hearts; rivers and mountains would not suffice to seal their oath.
translations.idiomatic: Neither metal and stone nor rivers and mountains could have bound their hearts and oaths more firmly.

sentences.zh: 及魏安之至城下，旬日而智力俱竭。

translations.literal: But when Wei An reached the walls, within ten days both wisdom and strength were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Yuchi Jiong reached the walls, within ten days both counsel and strength were spent.

sentences.zh: 委金湯而不守，舉庸蜀而來王。

translations.literal: He abandoned his golden ramparts and moats without defending them, and surrendered the whole of Yong and Shu to submit as a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned his impregnable defenses without a fight and surrendered all of Yong and Shu to submit as a vassal king.

sentences.zh: 若乃見機而作，誠有之矣。

translations.literal: As for acting when he saw the opportune moment, that he truly did.
translations.idiomatic: That he acted when he saw his moment—this much is true.

sentences.zh: 守節沒齒，則未可焉。

translations.literal: But to preserve his integrity to the end of his days—that cannot be granted.
translations.idiomatic: But to have held his integrity to the grave—that cannot be said.

sentences.zh: 宗懍幹局才辭見稱於梁元之世。

translations.literal: Zong Lin's practical ability and literary talent won praise in the age of Emperor Yuan of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Lin's practical ability and literary talent won praise under Emperor Yuan of Liang.

sentences.zh: 逮乎俘囚楚甸，播越秦中，屬太祖思治之辰，遇世宗好士之日，在朝不預政事，就列纔忝戎章。

translations.literal: Later, as a captive in the Chu region and a wanderer in Qin territory, he belonged to the age when the Grand Patriarch sought good government and met the days when Emperor Shizong loved scholars; at court he took no part in state affairs, and among the ranks he barely held a military title.
translations.idiomatic: Later, taken captive in the Chu region and cast adrift in Qin territory, he lived in the age when the Grand Patriarch sought good government and when Emperor Shizong loved men of talent; at court he took no part in government, and among the official ranks he barely held a military post.

sentences.zh: 豈懷道圖全，優遊卒歲，將用與不用，留滯當年乎？

translations.literal: Did he cherish the Way and seek to preserve himself whole, passing his years at ease—or was it rather a matter of being used or not used, and lingering on through those years?
translations.idiomatic: Did he cherish the Way and seek to preserve himself, passing his years at ease—or was it simply that he was used or not used, and so lingered on?

sentences.zh: 梁氏據有江東，五十餘載。

translations.literal: The house of Liang held the lands east of the Yangzi for more than fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Liang held the lands east of the Yangzi for more than fifty years.

sentences.zh: 挾策紀事，勒成不朽者，非一家焉。

translations.literal: Those who carried tablets to record events and carved them into imperishable works were not of a single school alone.
translations.idiomatic: Those who took up the brush to record events and set them down for posterity were not of one school alone.

sentences.zh: 劉璠學思通博，有著述之譽，雖傳疑傳信，頗有詳略，而屬辭比事，足為清典。

translations.literal: Liu Fan's learning and thought were broad and penetrating, and he enjoyed a reputation for authorship; although his work contains doubtful and credible passages alike and shows considerable unevenness of detail, in arranging words and comparing events it suffices as a clear standard.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fan's learning was broad and penetrating, and he enjoyed a reputation as an author; though his work mixes doubtful and credible passages and varies in detail, in arranging words and comparing events it stands as a clear standard.

sentences.zh: 蓋近代之佳史歟。

translations.literal: It may well be a fine history of recent times.
translations.idiomatic: It may well rank among the fine histories of recent times.

sentences.zh: 柳霞立身之道，進退有節。

translations.literal: Liu Xia's way of establishing himself in life showed moderation in advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xia's way of living showed moderation in when to advance and when to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 觀其眷戀墳隴，其孝可移於朝廷；

translations.literal: Observing his attachment to his ancestral tombs, his filial piety could be transferred to the court;
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his devotion to his ancestral tombs, one knows his filial piety could have served the court;

sentences.zh: 盡禮舊主，其忠可事於新君。

translations.literal: observing how he fulfilled every rite toward his former lord, his loyalty could have been offered to a new ruler.
translations.idiomatic: seeing how he fulfilled every obligation to his former lord, one knows his loyalty could have served a new ruler.

sentences.zh: 夫能推此類以求賢，則知人幾于易矣。

translations.literal: If one can extend this kind of example to seek the worthy, then knowing men is nearly easy.
translations.idiomatic: If rulers can extend such examples in seeking the worthy, then knowing men becomes almost easy.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》, November 1971.
translations.idiomatic: The complete text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971 edition).
